Peres Jepchirchir won the 2026 Sydney marathon by three minutes and 40 seconds

Reigning world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for a doping violation.

The 33-year-old, who also won Olympic gold in 2021, was provisionally suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) in October after an out-of-competition sample tested positive for erythropoietin (EPO).

The sample was collected in Kenya prior to Jepchirchir winning the Sydney Marathon on 30 August 2026 and returned an adverse finding on 17 September.

She is one of three high-profile Kenyan athletes to have been sanctioned. Veronica Loleo has also been banned for three years after admitting using EPO, while Ronald Korir has received a six-year ban after failing to explain abnormalities found in his biological passport.

EPO is a natural substance produced within the kidneys that stimulates the creation of new red blood cells.

If injected, it increases the amount of red blood cells, which carry oxygen to the muscles, in the blood stream but is only detectable in urine or blood for a short window of time.

Jepchirchir's other major wins came at the New York Marathon in 2021, the Boston Marathon in 2022 and the London Marathon in 2024.

While she denied using EPO, she signed an admission of violations form and accepted disqualification of all her competitive results since 17 July 2026.

"The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go," said Brett Clothier, chief executive of the AIU.

"The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country.

"We will discuss the details behind these commitments with the Kenyan government in the coming months."

South African DJ Lag says it is a "dream come true" to have his music featured on Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), the hugely popular video game released on Thursday.

DJ lag, one of South Africa's best-known electronic music producers, is among several African stars to feature, alongside Nigerian singers Burna Boy and Asake.

"I can't explain the feeling. I started playing the game last night and it's amazing," DJ Lag told the BBC's Newsday programme, adding that he had been playing GTA since he was about 10 years old and could hardly believe he was now part of the latest edition.

Many players have already had a chance to play the game following its worldwide launch .

The game, which lets players explore a fictional American city, features a dedicated African music radio station playing Afrobeats, amapiano and other sounds from across the continent.

The release of GTA 6 ends a 13-year wait for a new edition of the game.

GTA 6 is a satirical video series associated with crime and violence

Rockstar Games, the developer behind the franchise, has revealed details of the game's soundtrack and some in-game radio stations, but has yet to release a complete list of songs featured in the game.

Rockstar says AfroBank FM features everything from 20th Century African classics to contemporary amapiano and 3-step, giving the continent's music a prominent place in the latest edition.

Burna Boy co-hosts the station alongside British DJ and producer Palms Trax, while Asake's hit song Joha is among the tracks players can listen to as they drive around the game's virtual world.

DJ Lag, whose real name is Lwazi Asanda Gwala, is regarded as one of the pioneers of gqom, a genre of electronic dance music that emerged in the port city of Durban in the early 2010s.

Ghanaian highlife legends Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor also feature, alongside South African artists Robot Boii and Kamo Mphela, bringing a mix of classic and contemporary African music to one of gaming's biggest franchises.

Rockstar has also announced a 34-track official soundtrack album, released in partnership with Atlantic Records, featuring an original Burna Boy song titled Bigger.

For African fans, the inclusion of familiar music adds another dimension to the experience, allowing players to hear some of the continent's biggest sounds while exploring the American setting.

The series allows players to roam through sprawling fictional cities, drive vehicles and complete missions involving crime, police pursuits and other adventures.

The latest instalment takes players to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, and the surrounding US state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

Its story follows two criminals, Jason and Lucia, who become caught up in a wider conspiracy after a robbery goes wrong.

The launch has generated enormous excitement among gamers around the world.

Some fans downloaded it in advance so they could begin playing as soon as it became available, while others have booked leave from work.

The previous edition, GTA 5, was one of the best-selling video games of all time, selling more than 200 million copies worldwide.

The new release is expected to be another major commercial success, although it remains to be seen whether it will match its predecessor's extraordinary sales.

The assistant referee had a 60-day recovery period after being operated on

An Ecuadorian footballer has been banned for eight years for throwing a rock at an assistant referee, leaving him requiring surgery to his face.

Jhon Perlaza was playing for Club Ciudad de Yantzaza against Club Rio Aguarico FC in a third-tier match in October when the incident took place.

The stone struck assistant referee Lenin Giovanni Ojeda Nunez in the face in the 96th minute of the game, which was subsequently abandoned.

A video on social media shows Perlaza standing up in the team's dugout to throw the stone, with Nunez instantly falling to the floor and holding his face after the object hits him. He then receives medical attention.

"The assistant referee suffered serious injuries that required surgery and a 60-day recovery period," the Ecuadorian Football Federation (FEF) said.

"The disciplinary committee found the player responsible for physical aggression against a match official and suspended him for eight years from all football-related activity, until 19 October, 2034.

"In addition, the FEF will ask Fifa to extend this sanction worldwide."

The FEF also fined his club Yantzaza $2,000 (£1,521) and ordered them to pay Nunez's medical fees of $4,369 (£3,323).

In a statement released on 20 October, three days after the match, Yantzaza apologised to the refereeing team and the fans, and confirmed Perlaza had been sacked as a result of the incident.

"As an institution, we categorically reject all acts of aggression, whether verbal or physical, both inside and outside sporting venues. We firmly believe that football should be a space of respect, coexistence, and fair play," they said.

"Once the person responsible for this regrettable incident was identified, the institution made the decision to remove him immediately, and he is therefore no longer part of our club."

Itororokanirizo ry'amakuru AFP rimusubiramwo, yagize ati: "Umuntu ari ku nkengera z'ikiyaga yarashobora kwumva amaborogo y'abantu bari muri ubwo bwato."

AFP yatangaje ko umwe mu barokotse iryo sanganya abajijwe n'abapolisi yavuze ko ubwo bwato bwari butwaye abantu bashika 100.

Abapolisi basanze mu bisigarira vy'ubwo bwato impapuro ndangamuntu, amaterefone ngendanwa menshi hamwe n'ibindi vyari bitunze abari muri bwo. Muri ivyo, harimwo n'igikoresho co kw'ishure bikekwa ko cari ic'umunyeshure yiga mu mashure yisumbuye.

Mu nama y'abashikiranganji yabaye ku musi wa gatatu, Perezida Diomaye Faye yagaragaje impungenge ku bijanye n'ukwiyongera kw'ingendo zitemewe z'abimukira bava muri Sénégal, bizeye gushika i Buraya.

Yasavye ubushikiranganji bw'intwaro yo hagati gutegura icegeranyo gisuzuma imvo zituma abantu bafata izo ngendo zitera akaga, kikerekana n'ingingo zoshobora gufatwa kugira ico kibazo gitorerwe umuti.

Inyuma y'irindi sanganya ry'ubwato ryabaye mu kwezi guheze, Faye yari yahamagariye abanya Sénégal kutishira mu kaga ko guhitanwa n'urupfu mu kugerageza kujabuka ikiyaga.

Ishirahamwe mpuzamakungu rijejwe abimukira (IOM) ryavuze mu kwezi guheze ko ryari rimaze kwandika abantu nibura 454 bapfuye canke babuzwe irengero muri uyu mwaka gusa, bariko bagerageza guca mw'ibahari Atlantique, hafi y'inkengera zo mu Burengero bwa Afrika.

Iryo shirahamwe ryagabishije ko ico gitigiri gishobora kuba kiri munsi y'ic'ukuri, kuko hari ubwato bwinshi buzama ntihagire umuntu n'umwe arokoka canke ngo hasigare ikimenyetso na kimwe c'ivyabashikiye.

The band have become known for their energetic live performances and interwoven four-part harmonies

Westside Cowboy have been announced as BBC Introducing Artist of the Year 2026.

Jimmy Bradbury, Reuben Haycocks, Aoife Anson O'Connell and Paddy Murphy formed the band in Manchester in 2023 and have since rocketed from the pub circuit to some of the UK's biggest festivals.

The award is presented to an up-and-coming artist or band who has, with the support of BBC Introducing, made a significant impact and has previously been won by Olivia Dean, Myles Smith and Tom Grennan.

Murphy, from Longridge in Lancashire, said the win put them in "good company", with Bradbury, from Shropshire, adding that it was "very flattering".

BBC Introducing supports new musical talent across the UK , providing a platform to propel new artists on to the local and national stage through 30 Introducing shows, three national radio shows and six shows across BBC Radio 1, Radio 1Xtra, Radio 2, 6Music, Radio 3 and Asian Network.

About 72,000 tracks from emerging UK artists supported by BBC Introducing make it on to the airwaves each year.

Westside Cowboy uploaded their debut single I've Never Met Anyone I Thought I Could Really Love (Until I Met You) to the Introducing platform in November 2024 and had their first play on radio within hours.

Murphy and Bradbury were surprised with the award during a radio interview

The four-piece played in various other bands before coming together to form Westside Cowboy.

Haycocks, O'Connell, and Murphy had met at Manchester's Royal Northern College of Music in 2021 and later got to know Bradbury after meeting him in the nearby Johnny Roadhouse music shop.

Murphy and Bradbury played in surf-rock trio Katz, while Murphy and Haycocks both worked together in noise-pop trio, DieKaiDie, but it was when Bradbury, who was working in the music shop repairing guitars, asked the others if they wanted to start a new band that Westside Cowboy's journey began.

By the time their second single, Shells, was released in April 2025, they had been been selected to play the BBC Introducing stage at Glastonbury Festival, and the song was put on the BBC 6Music playlist.

Their meteoric rise saw seen them appear on BBC music show Later... with Jools Holland in June and their debut album It Goes On was released on Island Records in August, peaking at number five in the UK charts.

Westside Cowboy reminisced about the early days on BBC Radio Manchester

Thanking the Introducing network and listeners for their support, Murphy said it was "really cool to be recognised for the music you make".

"We say this a lot, so apologies if we sound like a broken record, [but] it's funny with this band because... we started it with so little pretence or plan," he said.

"So whenever people give us something cool like [this award], it's all a bit surreal because it still feels like a weekend project that we now just get to do way more regularly.

"We're very lucky it's one of those things.

Westside Cowboy formed in 2023, having played together in other bands

William Wolstenholme, presenter and producer of BBC Introducing in Lancashire & Cumbria, gave the band their first play and said he remembers messaging them to upload the track.

"Over the past two years, Westside Cowboy have become surely the most exciting band in Manchester, and therefore the country," he said.

"They've fast-tracked from the sweaty pubs of the city's student music scene to many of the most famous venues in the country.

"It's a rise whose speed can scarcely be believed, and one that has shocked much of the music industry."

He said the band's obvious camaraderie was one of their main selling points.

"They're still the same four mates wandering down Oxford Road in Manchester, and the reason the music has resonated with so many people is because it's a true reflection of those four kids," he said.

"They've been themselves and, in doing so, have brought the fashion and style of the past 10 years of UK post-punk culture down to earth."

Ni ibyaha yakoreye i Nyanza mu Ntara y'Amajyepfo, abatangabuhamya babajijwe bakaba baragarutse cyane kuri bariyeli yari i Nyanza hafi y'ahitwa kwa Premier, hiciwe abatutsi benshi aho Madjaliwa ashinjwa kubigiramo uruhare.

Ashinjwa uruhare mu rupfu rw'abantu batandukanye ndetse by'umwihariko mu bwicanyi bwibasiye Abakono.

Umutangabuhamya Florent Piton ni we mutangabuhamya wasobanuye amakuru atuma Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi yumvikana, temoin de contexte.

Yerekanye ko kwica Abatutsi byatangiye mu 1959, biza kuba Jenoside mu 1994.

Mu ba avoka bahagarariye abarega - parties civiles, Emma Sabadotto yagaragaje ko mu myumvire ishingiye ku macakubiri yerekeye abagore b’Abatutsi, harimo igitekerezo cy’uko bagira imiterere y’umubiri utemba itoto, bakagira n'uburanga butangaje bukurura abagabo.

Umutangabuhamya yahise yerekeza ku nomero ya 6 y’ikinyamakuru KANGURA, yasohoye “Amategeko Icumi y’Abahutu” (Les dix commandements des Bahutu). Muri ayo mategeko, harimo irivuga ko:

“Abahutu batagomba kugwa mu mutego w’abagore b’Abatutsi bashobora kuyobya abagabo b’Abahutu, bakoresheje ubwiza n’uburanga bwabo kugira ngo babigarurire, babatere gushyigikira inyungu z’Abatutsi.”

Yasoje asobanura ko iki kimenyetso gifasha kugaragaza ko ifatwa ku ngufu ryakorewe abagore b’Abatutsi ryari kimwe mu bigize umugambi wa Jenoside. Aha, yerekana ko iryo fatwa ku ngufu ryatijwe umurindi n'iyo sura bari barambitse umugore wo mu bwoko bw'Abatutsi.

Impuzamashyirahamwe y’Umupira w’Amaguru ku Isi (FIFA) yatangaje ko yakiriye kandidatire ebyiri z’abifuza guhatana na Gianni Infantino ku mwanya wa Perezida w’uyu muryango mu matora ateganyijwe mu 2027. Abo ni Philippe Diallo ukomoka mu Bufaransa, uyobora Ishyirahamwe ry’Umupira w’Amaguru muri icyo gihugu (FFF), na Kohzo Tashima wo mu Buyapani, wahoze ayobora Ishyirahamwe ry’Umupira w’Amaguru muri icyo gihugu akaba uyu munsi ari Perezida waryo w’icyubahiro.

Aba bombi bazahatana na Gianni Infantino usanzwe ayobora FIFA kuva mu 2016, akaba ashaka kongera gutorerwa indi manda.

Amatora ateganyijwe ku wa 18 Werurwe 2027, azabera i Rabat muri Maroc, mu nama ya 77 ya FIFA izahuza abanyamuryango b’uyu muryango baturutse mu bihugu 211.

FIFA yatangaje ko kandidatire zatanzwe zashyikirijwe Komisiyo ishinzwe amatora kugira ngo zisuzumwe, harebwe niba abazitanze bujuje ibisabwa kugira ngo bemererwe kwiyamamaza. Umwanzuro wa nyuma ku bazemererwa kuzahatana uteganyijwe gutangazwa bitarenze ku wa 18 Gashyantare 2027.

Aya matora azaba afite umwihariko kuko Infantino agiye guhatanira kuyobora FIFA ahanganye n’abandi bakandida, mu gihe mu matora yo mu 2023 yari yiyamamaje nta wundi muhanganye. Kohzo Tashima na Philippe Diallo kandidatire zabo nizemezwa burundu, bazaba bafite akazi gakomeye ko guhangana na Infantino usanzwe afite ubunararibonye n’umubano ukomeye n’amashyirahamwe menshi y’umupira w’amaguru ku isi.

A consultant surgeon at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary has called for a corporate homicide investigation into claims of the unavoidable deaths of NHS Grampian patients over many years.

Dr Mohammed Habib, who is still a surgeon at the hospital, said he had been raising concerns for a decade, including with government ministers and police but he had been ignored.

The whistleblowing medic also leaked an unpublished expert review from 2022 which found 19 avoidable deaths among 45 patients in liver and pancreatic surgery, including some who bled to death in the operating theatre because of mistakes by surgeons.

The allegations come a week after a scathing report found poor leadership and culture at the NHS Grampian board. The board's management is yet to comment on these latest public claims.

Dr Mohammed Habib has been raising concerns for a decade

Last week, Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS) found "major deficiencies" across the region and revealed that a failure to learn from mistakes had caused "repeated and avoidable harm" to patients.

Health Secretary Angela Constance insisted that patients were safe and said she would demand "full transparency" at every level.

Habib, who has been a consultant with NHS Grampian since 2014, held a media conference on Thursday and said he was putting his career on the line to demand accountability from the health board.

The consultant said he formally reported serious concerns about dozens of avoidable deaths in 2021.

In 2024, he reported 20 cases from the previous decade to the police but no charges have been brought.

He has also leaked two reports by external experts which examined surgical care in NHS Grampian.

A 2022 review looked at 45 patients in the care of liver and pancreatic services at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (ARI) between 2015 and 2021.

It said 31 had died, and 19 of them were considered to have died of avoidable consequences of surgery or intervention.

The 2022 review criticised decision-making in liver surgery for occasionally being "overly aggressive", with surgery going ahead even if the disease was thought to be inoperable.

In pancreatic surgery, patients were regularly rushed into theatre without adequate planning or consideration of non-surgical alternatives, the experts said.

The review said blood losses in both surgeries was "unacceptably high" and said there was a lack of leadership and no clear standards for planning before operations.

It said poor decision-making and aggressive strategies were adopted despite high levels of deaths being predicted.

A second report earlier earlier this year raised similar themes, with poor judgement about the risks and benefits of operating and repeated examples of massive blood losses and deaths during and after surgery.

It said it was clear that problems in the unit were "long standing and recurrent", adding that NHS Grampian had tried to improve outcomes but had not made the structural changes needed.

It noted that the unit did not have enough specialist staff to deliver the service safely, and that despite concerns being raised repeatedly since 2010, the issues had not been dealt with.

It strongly recommended that no complex or major HPB (Hepatopancreatobiliary) surgery should take place at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary.

Dr Habib, who has worked in General Surgery & HPB (liver, pancreas and bile duct) since 2014, said he thought several hundred patients had come to harm from an excessively high rate of complications.

He said he had tried his best to use the whistleblowing procedures but the institutions he had contacted had failed to act as robustly as they should have.

He said he first became about avoidable surgery-related deaths in 2016.

In July 2021, he formally raised serious concerns about what he believes were dozens of avoidable deaths.

In February 2024, he spoke to Police Scotland.

Habib said he believes NHS Grampian was guilty of "wicked recklessness and an indifference to patient deaths".

The consultant said the 2022 external expert report, which was never made public, concluded that 19 deaths out of a case study of 45 were avoidable (42%).

He said he had contacted the first minister and health secretary on numerous occasions since June 2023 but the Scottish government had said it had "no jurisdiction" to investigate whistleblowing claims.

Habib also said that the Independent Whistleblowing Officer (INWO) refused to progress his complaints on the basis that they were either "time barred".

He also wrote to the chief executive of NHS Grampian, Laura Skaife Knight, in December 2025.

She replied: "I would be grateful if you can let HIS complete it enquiries rather than continuing to correspond with me about these matters, as I have nothing further to add to this response at this stage."

Habib said: "They are avoiding accountability by not being transparent about what damage has been done, while promising heaven and earth going forward."

Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni and Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan have agreed to accelerate preparations for a Standard Gauge Railway that would connect Isaka in Tanzania to Mpondwe, on Uganda’s border with the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The leaders witnessed the signing of a framework agreement at State House in Entebbe on November 18, during Hassan’s two-day state visit.

The proposed line would pass through Lusahunga and Murongo/Kikagati before reaching Mpondwe. The presidents said it could improve regional trade, cut transport costs and open a new rail gateway to eastern DRC.

They directed their governments to speed up feasibility studies, technical designs and financing plans. The project’s cost and construction timetable have not yet been established.

The railway is planned to reach the Ugandan border; onward rail links into eastern DRC would be needed to connect the Congolese market directly.

Earlier tripartite discussions and a route survey involving Uganda, Tanzania and DRC laid groundwork for the proposal, with the African Development Bank supporting project preparation.

For Tanzania, the line could extend the Central Corridor and strengthen the role of Dar es Salaam port. Uganda would gain another route to regional markets and a potential corridor for goods moving between DRC and the coast.

The railway is part of wider Uganda–Tanzania infrastructure cooperation. The leaders also welcomed progress on the 1,443-kilometre East African Crude Oil Pipeline, which they reported was 93.9% complete, and called for the development of Tanga as a regional energy hub.

Simba Supermarket has opened its 16th branch in Kabuga, continuing its expansion as it seeks to bring its services to more communities across Rwanda.

Patrice Ndanga, Executive Secretary of Rusororo Sector, attended the opening and presented Simba Suppermarket with a trophy in recognition of the company’s corporate social responsibility work in the area.

The Kabuga launch follows several recent additions to Simba’s network. The company opened its 13th branch in Rubavu in March 2025, complementing its Musanze outlet, and has also expanded in Kigali, including in Gahanga and Nyamirambo.

Its branches sell groceries, fresh produce, bakery items and household goods, and the company also offers online shopping.

Speaking on Thursday, chief executive Teklay Teame said Rwanda’s business environment was helping the company grow. “The business environment created by our government is helping us expand,” he said.

The expansion comes after a fire swept through GOICO Plaza in Musanze in October. Simba’s branch was spared, and all staff were safe.

Rwanda is stepping up efforts to attract high-spending international visitors and strengthen its position as a premium tourism destination through its participation in Luxperience 2026, a luxury travel trade event taking place in Sydney, Australia, from November 17 to 20.

The four-day event brings together leading luxury tourism buyers, travel advisors and industry players from Australia, New Zealand and other international markets, offering the country an opportunity to promote its exclusive travel experiences and establish business relationships with influential players in the global tourism industry.

The delegation is led by Rwanda Development Board (RDB) Chief Tourism Officer Irène Murerwa and includes local tour operators and travel agents, in collaboration with the Rwandan High Commission in Singapore.

Their participation is aimed at showcasing the country’s high-end tourism offerings, attracting new travel partnerships and increasing its visibility among affluent travellers across the Asia-Pacific region.

Rwanda has increasingly positioned itself as a luxury tourism destination, building its appeal around high-end accommodation, wildlife experiences, conservation tourism and personalised travel services.

Among its flagship attractions is gorilla trekking in Volcanoes National Park, an experience that draws international visitors willing to pay premium prices for close encounters with endangered mountain gorillas in their natural habitat.

Other experiences include wildlife safaris in Akagera National Park, chimpanzee tracking and canopy walks in Nyungwe National Park, as well as leisure and cultural tourism around Lake Kivu.

By presenting these experiences to international luxury travel buyers, the delegation hopes to encourage travel companies to include the destination in their premium holiday packages and recommend it to clients seeking exclusive and distinctive African experiences.

The participation also carries significant economic opportunities for the country.

Australia, New Zealand and the wider Asia-Pacific region represent potential source markets for visitors who can contribute to tourism revenues through premium accommodation, guided excursions, domestic transport, hospitality and other tourism-related services.

Securing partnerships with established international travel advisors could help generate more bookings, increase visitor spending and extend the benefits of tourism to local businesses, including hotels, tour operators, transport providers, restaurants and community-based tourism initiatives.

The expansion into these markets could also help diversify the country’s international visitor base, reducing its reliance on traditional source markets while strengthening its competitiveness in the global luxury travel industry.

Beyond attracting visitors, international exposure at events such as Luxperience provides an opportunity to build confidence among overseas travel companies and position the country as a destination capable of delivering high-quality, personalised and sustainable tourism experiences.

The involvement of local tour operators and travel agents is also important in ensuring that international partnerships translate into direct business opportunities for domestic tourism companies.

Through its tourism promotion strategy, the country has continued to prioritise high-value, low-impact tourism, with conservation and premium visitor experiences forming key pillars of its approach.

Participation in Luxperience 2026 therefore offers another opportunity to connect its tourism ambitions with international demand, particularly among travellers seeking exclusive wildlife encounters, nature-based holidays and luxury experiences in Africa.

After years of anticipation and delays, as well as controversy around worker rights, Grand Theft Auto 6 has completed its phased worldwide release and is available to gamers everywhere, including the UK.

There has been near universal praise from critics, with review aggregator Metacritic calculating its average score at 99 out of 100 based on 150 reviews. , external

Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has held the top spot since 1998 - but Metacritic confirmed to the BBC that this has now officially been overtaken.

GTA 6 is set to become one of the world's most popular entertainment products ever, with fans booking time off work, and schools warning students not to bunk off.

Some schools have reminded parents and pupils to prioritise study over the game, which has an 18 rating , external for "strong graphic violence, strong sexual themes and use of illegal drugs".

One school in Essex incentivised pupils to attend with prize s such as vouchers, Christmas dinners and a pass to skip the lunch queue.

The UK rating means it can only be legally sold to an adult. It does not stop an adult letting their child play the game - instead it is meant to inform their decision.

It's the game that shocked and thrilled the world: Grand Theft Auto. As a new installment is released in 2026, go deep into the history of the game with rapper Bugzy Malone.

The game, set in the fictional US state of Leonida, follows two protagonists, Lucia and Jason, through the seedy underbelly of America after an "easy score goes wrong".

It was released at midnight in all the countries it is available in, which meant New Zealanders were the first to access it.

"The graphics are great. Even from the set-up and credits, it's feeling pretty good," Aleana Fernando, who lives in Auckland, New Zealand, told BBC Newsbeat soon after she started playing.

Once the game was released at midnight UK time, gamers were equally enthralled by the game's graphics and attention to detail.

Charlie Wood from London said he had "already laughed at the dialogue before even stepping into the gameplay".

About 30 minutes into playing in Leonida, he said it was "most definitely worth the wait".

The Guardian's Keza MacDonald , external was impressed by the relationship between the main characters.

"GTA has never been particularly kind to women... there is still a lot of sexism in GTA VI's world, but now we have Lucia to react to it," she said.

"This is the first GTA in which I have felt the women are treated as people, not only Lucia but also the many other female characters in the story".

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics

After GTA 5 became one of the most successful entertainment products of all time - with estimates of net profits soaring as high up as $10bn (£7.6bn) - anticipation could not be higher for the sixth instalment.

Makers Rockstar North, headquartered in Edinburgh, delayed the release twice, saying it needed extra months to finish the game with the level of polish fans had come to "expect and deserve".

The company was also set back by hacks and leaks of its unfinished version.

On Monday, 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, pleaded guilty to the Rockstar Games hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished and hugely anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6.

A group of Rockstar workers who were sacked by the company have also been protesting outside its offices, ahead of a tribunal which heard they were penalised for discussing working conditions in a private online forum while working on the game.

They claimed they were punished for being part of a workers' union, but Thomas Cordrey, representing Rockstar, said employees made disparaging comments about the company on a semi-public Discord server and shared confidential information.

Tech Now's Laura Cress previews GTA 6 with the game's original creators

Players were able to download the 212GB game ahead of time, in order to be able to play it as soon as it was made available.

Some had even gone to the lengths of buying a whole new console dedicated to the game.

Broadband providers Virgin Media O2, as well as BT and EE, said internet traffic records had been broken in the days leading up to the UK release.

The BBC has heard from people planning to take time off work - as well as a company which has given its employees the day off - in order to dedicate time to the game.

Kieran Youens-Byrne, 34, from Manchester said he was "going on a pilgrimage to Wales" where he would be "completely off grid" for a week.

He added his partner Clare "has been incredibly understanding, although I suspect she's questioning why our romantic getaway revolves around a PlayStation".

Florence Pugh attended the Governors Awards in Hollywood at the weekend

Florence Pugh has said she was "disturbed" to see "thousands of people" discussing her recent appearance at the Governors Awards, and denied speculation about weight-loss drugs and facial surgery.

The actress wrote on Instagram , external how stressful" it was waking up to people "talking about you and your body in ways that you can't even comprehend".

"I have never been on Ozempic. I have never done any face surgery," she wrote. "And don't ever say that I didn't make my own nose, I've always had that beautiful ski slope. Even as a baby!"

She added: "For the first time in my entire career, I have had the opportunity to be rested, to sleep, to wake up and work out and to eat regularly and healthily."

In her eight-page statement, the Oppenheimer, Dune and East of Eden star told followers: "I'm looking after myself, and that's literally it."

Pugh has spoken out before about judgement about how women look

Pugh highlighted that losing weight had not been her goal, and she had lost "two pounds".

"The thing that's most important to me and my trainer is muscle," she said. "I think it's the most important thing a woman can do. Build muscle and be strong. I can now do six pull-ups and lift 110kg.

"Which I'm sure to many of you isn't a lot... but to me?! It's everything."

The actress said that from the moment she entered the acting industry she was "subjected to fat shaming".

"I have loved every time I get to tell someone they are being inappropriate about my weight, and I'm not changing that now just because you've all said so."

She also said she was "disturbed" that "women who now think that I'm someone I'm not, for having my body dissected and pointed at again".

"I have spent my whole career defending and protecting bodies that just grow the way they grow."

Pugh is no stranger to a striking red carpet outfit

Pugh, who was Oscar-nominated for Little Women in 2020 and played Black Widow assassin Yelena Belova in this year's Spider-Man: Brand New Day, has previously spoken out against judgement about women's looks.

In 2024, she told the Times , external she aimed to "challenge how women were perceived".

"Look, not everybody has legs that go on for days. I remember watching this industry and feeling that I wasn't represented," she said. "I've loved challenging ideas I don't like."

She also spoke about why she thinks she receives criticism about her appearance.

"I've always been aware that seeing a confident woman be happy in her skin is triggering to a lot of people and for a long time just accepted that I will receive commentary like that," she said.

"But now this...? I'm asking us all to just be mindful. We are real people, living real lives."

Pugh did not have comments turned on for her post, but it was liked by celebrities including Ashley James, who is known for speaking out about body positivity, plus Carol Vorderman, Zoe Ball, writer and actress Katy Brand and doctor and broadcaster Amir Khan.

Pugh also said she had sued several publications earlier this year, claiming they published AI-generated images appearing to show her receiving cosmetic injections that were presented as real photographs.

"I was... horrified," she wrote, claiming the articles had damaged her reputation.

The actress concluded by urging followers to think about their attitudes towards physical appearance.

"I understand that we are in a warped part of image history right now, with beauty standards changing, getting harder and harder to keep up with," she said.

"But please be gentle to yourselves and others when you go in on people's physical appearance.

"I'm not angry at you, I'm angry at the situation that's being projected onto us.

"It feels inescapable, but part of changing the tide is on you as much as us in the public eye."

Ticket-reselling site Viagogo may have broken the law on hidden fees, the UK's competition body has said in a provisional finding.

The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) said it found that Viagogo failed to show consumers the total price upfront when they were buying tickets "and added fees later in the process, a practice known as drip pricing".

The CMA added that this was an initial finding, and it should not be assumed that the company had actually broken the law.

In a statement, Viagogo said it was co-operating fully with the CMA, adding that the investigation was continuing and "no final findings have been made".

The CMA said last year that it was investigating a number of companies over their online pricing practices, including Viagogo.

The competition watchdog said it had looked into the experience of UK fans buying tickets for events such as concerts and sport on three websites that operate under the Viagogo brand.

"The CMA believes that mandatory costs such as taxes and booking fees were added at later stages of the checkout process and not included in the total price from the start," it said.

"Drip pricing can cause fans to be caught out by extra charges and buy tickets they might not otherwise have selected, had they been able to compare prices accurately from the start."

The CMA said Viagogo would now have an opportunity to consider its findings and respond before a final decision is made.

"This is an ongoing investigation and no final findings have been made," Viagogo said in a statement.

"We have engaged constructively with the CMA and continue to cooperate fully with its investigation."

The CMA has powers to tackle anti-competitive behaviour. It can now decide if consumer laws have been broken - rather than having to go through the courts.

Drip pricing is one of the practices the CMA has been focusing on particularly.

On Wednesday, it said it was investigating three companies , external over the issue, and in August it announced that the Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School had been engaged in the practice.

Ella Langley said her hit Choosin' Texas was "the gift that keeps on giving"

US singer Ella Langley has swept the Country Music Association Awards (CMAs), following the huge success of her breakthrough hit Choosin' Texas.

The Alabama-born singer was named entertainer of the year at Wednesday's ceremony, weeks after the song became the longest-running number one in Billboard chart history.

"At this point, I'm sick of me," the 27-year-old joked in her acceptance speech, having spent so much of the ceremony on stage. "I could quit tomorrow and have the best career of my life."

Choosin' Texas was also named single of the year and song of the year, leading Langley to joke in an acceptance speech: "This song is the gift that keeps on giving."

Ella Langley, who won six awards on the night, performed her song Loving Life Again

Langley won six awards in total, including female vocalist of the year, music video of the year and album of the year for Dandelion.

She also performed her song Loving Life Again with a string quartet, and duetted with Miranda Lambert for a performance of Snakeskin Boots.

Choosin' Texas made history in September after spending 23 weeks at the top spot on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. It has now spent 28 weeks in total at the summit.

Following her win, Langley took to social media and said: "Hard to put this night into words and what it means.

"Thank you to my fans. Thank you for loving this record, thank you for coming to my shows, thank you for believing in my artistry.

"This year has been the most incredible journey, and I want to thank you for sharing in that with me. I love y'all."

Langley also performed Snakeskin Boots with Miranda Lambert during the ceremony

Taylor Swift also performed at the CMA Awards for the first time in 13 years.

Her performance began with Swift walking backstage and featured cameo appearances from country stars including Brad Paisley, Little Big Town, Sugarland, and Brooks & Dunn.

Swift then sang her recent hit I Knew It, I Knew You, from the Toy Story 5 soundtrack, using a blue guitar with bedazzled clouds on it, in a nod to the animated franchise.

The singer also mixed in some of her 2006 country hit Our Song, while Keith Urban joined her on the banjo.

Taylor Swift used a Toy Story-themed guitar and performed alongside Keith Urban

She also presented a lifetime achievement award to country music duo Brooks & Dunn

Swift's performance came after she was inducted into both the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame and the Songwriters Hall of Fame earlier this year.

Other winners on the night included Chris Stapleton who won male vocalist of the year, The Red Clay Strays who won vocal group of the year, and Brooks & Dunn with vocal duo of the year.

Meanwhile Stephen Wilson Jr won the new artist of the year award while Charlie Worsham won musician of the year.

The award ceremony began with a tribute to country music legend Dolly Parton, who died in August aged 80.

Ceremony host Lainey Wilson began the tribute by duetting with singer-songwriter Vince Gill on a rendition of Parton's I Will Always Love You.

Presenters at the ceremony included actor Glen Powell and Shaboozey

There was also a firey performance of Who Told You That during the ceremony from Tucker Wetmore

Rwanda is seeking to strengthen its partnership with the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) to improve maternal and child healthcare services and expand investments in human capital development, as both sides look to build on four decades of cooperation.

The commitment was discussed during a meeting between Minister of Health Dr Sabin Nsanzimana and Etleva Kadilli, UNICEF Regional Director for Eastern and Southern Africa, who explored areas of continued collaboration in improving health outcomes for mothers and children.

Discussions focused on UNICEF’s contribution to the country’s healthcare system over the past 40 years, particularly its support for maternal and child health services and initiatives aimed at strengthening community capacity.

The partnership has played a role in supporting efforts to improve access to essential healthcare services, promote child well-being and strengthen the capacity of communities to address health and development challenges.

Looking ahead, the discussions highlighted the importance of sustaining cooperation to address emerging healthcare needs, strengthen community-level interventions and ensure that investments in maternal and child health translate into long-term improvements in human capital.

Speaking on the importance of the partnership, Dr Nsanzimana said:

“Our partnership with UNICEF remains important in strengthening maternal and child health services and building the capacity of our communities. Investing in the health and well-being of mothers and children is essential to developing a healthier and more productive population.”

The meeting comes as UNICEF marks 80 years of global operations and 40 years of working with the East African country.

Over the decades, the organisation has supported programmes targeting children’s rights, healthcare, nutrition, education and protection, working alongside government institutions and communities to improve living conditions.

The anniversary also provides an opportunity for both sides to reflect on achievements and identify priorities for the next phase of cooperation, particularly as human capital development remains central to the country’s long-term development ambitions.

Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Olivier Nduhungirehe, has called on Rwandans living in Norway to maintain strong ties with their home country and use their skills, expertise and investment opportunities to support its development.

Nduhungirehe made the appeal during a meeting with approximately 70 Rwandans living in Norway and friends of the country, held on the sidelines of his participation in a ministerial meeting bringing together foreign affairs ministers from Nordic and African countries.

During the engagement, the Minister briefed participants on the country’s development journey, highlighting achievements made across different sectors as well as emerging opportunities for investment and cooperation.

He encouraged members of the diaspora to go beyond maintaining their connection with their homeland by actively contributing to national development through knowledge-sharing, professional experience, business networks and investment.

“I encourage Rwandans living in Norway to continue working closely with their home country, using their knowledge, experience, networks and investment opportunities to contribute to Rwanda’s development,” he said.

The meeting aimed to strengthen engagement between the Government and the Rwandan diaspora, while exploring ways in which citizens abroad and friends of the country can support national priorities.

Rwandans living abroad are considered an important development partner through their professional expertise, financial contributions, international connections and potential investments.

The engagement also provided an opportunity for participants to learn more about developments at home and identify avenues through which they can contribute to the country’s continued economic and social transformation.

Impuzamashyirahamwe y’Umupira w’Amaguru ku Isi (FIFA) yatangaje ko yakiriye kandidatire ebyiri z’abifuza guhatana na Gianni Infantino ku mwanya wa Perezida w’uyu muryango mu matora ateganyijwe mu 2027. Abo ni Philippe Diallo ukomoka mu Bufaransa, uyobora Ishyirahamwe ry’Umupira w’Amaguru muri icyo gihugu (FFF), na Kohzo Tashima wo mu Buyapani, wahoze ayobora Ishyirahamwe ry’Umupira w’Amaguru muri icyo gihugu akaba uyu munsi ari Perezida waryo w’icyubahiro.

Aba bombi bazahatana na Gianni Infantino usanzwe ayobora FIFA kuva mu 2016, akaba ashaka kongera gutorerwa indi manda.

Amatora ateganyijwe ku wa 18 Werurwe 2027, azabera i Rabat muri Maroc, mu nama ya 77 ya FIFA izahuza abanyamuryango b’uyu muryango baturutse mu bihugu 211.

FIFA yatangaje ko kandidatire zatanzwe zashyikirijwe Komisiyo ishinzwe amatora kugira ngo zisuzumwe, harebwe niba abazitanze bujuje ibisabwa kugira ngo bemererwe kwiyamamaza. Umwanzuro wa nyuma ku bazemererwa kuzahatana uteganyijwe gutangazwa bitarenze ku wa 18 Gashyantare 2027.

Aya matora azaba afite umwihariko kuko Infantino agiye guhatanira kuyobora FIFA ahanganye n’abandi bakandida, mu gihe mu matora yo mu 2023 yari yiyamamaje nta wundi muhanganye. Kohzo Tashima na Philippe Diallo kandidatire zabo nizemezwa burundu, bazaba bafite akazi gakomeye ko guhangana na Infantino usanzwe afite ubunararibonye n’umubano ukomeye n’amashyirahamwe menshi y’umupira w’amaguru ku isi.

MN202611_1w4g79j93qd.t:
Early efforts to contain coronavirus "were doomed to fail" because the test, trace and isolate system in the UK could only handle a relatively small number of cases, the seventh report of the Covid inquiry says in a damning assessment.

Across 245 pages the inquiry looks at everything from border controls to how well contact tracing worked.

The report said the virus was allowed to spread virtually unchecked in the first few months after community testing and contact tracing was abandoned in mid-March 2020, costing lives.

Ministers said this was because testing capacity was being overwhelmed.

NHS Test and Trace was launched two months later and eventually became one of the biggest testing services in the world per head of population.

In the end, more than £30bn was spent across the UK during the pandemic on testing, tracing and isolating.

But in those early months the four UK nations were "effectively blind" to how quickly Covid was spreading, the inquiry said.

It criticises the government for not having a robust test, trace and isolate system in place to start with, saying this, alongside other failures, meant harsher measures, including lockdown and school closures, were needed.

Inquiry chair Baroness Hallett said the UK should have been better prepared and learnt lessons from other countries that had experience of dealing with outbreaks of other infectious diseases, such as Sars.

Unlike the UK, places such as Hong Kong, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan had established systems ready to go.

This was despite the fact the UK had run a series of simulation exercises in the years leading up to Covid.

It included Exercise Cygnus into a flu pandemic and Exercise Alice into Mers. Both identified problems relating to test, trace or isolation, which appear not to have been fully acted on.

The report also raises the question of whether the government could have made use of non-government testing facilities in hospitals, universities and the private sector from the start, instead of just relying on 12 government labs.

When people in the UK were told to isolate, "many felt forgotten and let down by the lack of practical or financial support when trying to follow the rules", says the report.

In the early months of the pandemic, estimates suggested less than half of people were complying with the rules around isolating if infected.

Ministers and their advisers discussed this and fines of up to £10,000 were introduced for those who did not comply, which some experts have said was counter-productive.

Changes were made to allow people to claim statutory sick pay.

But it was not until September in England – and later in Scotland and Wales – that £500 financial payments were introduced to help those on low incomes comply.

More also needed to be done to provide practical support for things such as collecting medicines and shopping for food for those who did not have people to call on.

Suspending all flights from China to the UK in February 2020 could "have provided valuable additional time to prepare healthcare systems for the impact of the pandemic", said inquiry chair Baroness Hallett. That didn't happen.

The report says the UK lacked a clear strategy for implementing border control measures early in the pandemic, which left the country in an "extremely vulnerable position".

Although the closure and restriction of borders was noted as "immensely complex", the inquiry said that border control measures could serve as an important tool "to reassure the public and increase confidence."

By April 2020, 93% of countries had put measures in place, such as flight suspensions, border closures and travel restrictions, to control their international borders.

By contrast, the UK government only requested travellers arriving from high-risk areas to self-isolate for 14 days. The UK government implemented no further border control measures until June 2020.

The report says that border controls were a "critical gap in the UK's ability to limit the spread of the virus" and recommends that in the future "international border control measures should be in place at the earliest stages of a pandemic".

The inquiry report is more positive about the use of smartphone apps, saying digital tools can have a "significant impact on reducing the spread of infection".

It quotes a mathematical modelling study from the US which estimates that, when 75% of people used a contact tracing app in the pandemic, infections were reduced by at least 50%.

Three different apps were developed during Covid - one for England and Wales, another for Scotland and a third for Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.

The inquiry says that took up "valuable time", and it recommends developing a UK-wide digital tool to use in any future outbreak.

It says it is "fundamentally important" that apps and digital tools are as accurate as possible – and people have confidence in them.

In the summer of 2021, as Covid restrictions were relaxed, around 7% of all UK adults were told to self-isolate over a seven-day period, something dubbed by the press as the "pingdemic".

It quotes Treasury estimates suggesting that may have reduced economic growth by as much as 0.3% that month.

MN202611_10c4etzwc8l.t:
The top five teams in the Championship are separated by just one point

Many supporters often like to label the Championship "the best league in the world".

It might be a throwaway comment, but it is one founded on the premise that the level of unpredictability and drama is unmatched.

And there is a case to be made that the Championship is living up to its unofficial tag more than ever this season.

We have seen astonishing comebacks, goals galore, unexpected results - and one third of the way through the 2026-27 campaign, you could throw a blanket over the top half of the table.

With just one point between the top five sides and eight points separating leaders Birmingham City down to Blackburn Rovers in 13th after 15 games, is this shaping up to be one of, if not the best promotion and play-off contests ever in the second tier?

A total of 12 different teams have been in a Championship play-off spot since gameweek four

"This is going to be fun," said 72+ EFL podcast host Aaron Paul.

Jobi McAnuff, who won the Championship with Reading in 2011-12, agrees.

"It's been a brilliant start of the season. I think there's such a lovely open nature to the league so far," McAnuff said.

"You certainly wouldn't have expected West Brom right up there. Stoke... Mark Robins again doing brilliantly, and Birmingham sitting top of the table."

Former Bromley manager Andy Woodman described it as "anyone's league".

"This Championship is relentless," Woodman said. "I'm looking at all the clubs in there and Scott Parker's record of getting out of the league. He's now at West Ham sitting just behind them ready to come up.

"It is going to be an unbelievable finish to the season and if we were to call it, I don't think we could."

The final game before the two-week international break epitomised just how close the race is, and gives us plenty of reason for excitement when the Championship returns this weekend.

It is usually a rare and precious moment when football fans are able to serenade their heroes with 'We are top of the league' on the terraces.

But no less than four sets of supporters were able to do so in the space of a few hours on the afternoon of Saturday, 7 November.

The name at the top of the table changed eight times between 12:54 GMT and 16:51 GMT that day, with Birmingham eventually securing pole position.

That was only after Wolves , Stoke and Middlesbrough had led the way, however briefly, earlier in the day.

The table after 15 games is as tight as it has been since Opta started compiling statistics in 2004, although there is one other season in which just one point separated the top five sides beyond this point in a campaign, and boy, was it a doozy.

In early March 2015 Roy Hodgson was still England manager and Prime Minister David Cameron led a Conservative/Lib Dem coalition in Westminster.

Meanwhile, 36 games into the Championship season, this is what the title race looked like...

Bournemouth and Watford won automatic promotion in 2014-15, with Norwich going up via the play-offs

Bournemouth went on to pick up 24 points from their final 10 games to win the title and promotion to the top flight for the first time with 90 points, one ahead of Watford, who also went up.

Norwich and Middlesbrough had to settle for the play-offs, finishing third and fourth on 86 and 85 points respectively, while Brentford and Ipswich sneaked into the play-offs on goal difference, with Wolves missing out after also finishing on 78 points.

Derby ended up in eighth after taking only 17 points from their final 10 games to miss the play-offs by a point.

The table only tells half the story, however.

The Hornets would have been champions had they not conceded a late equaliser against Sheffield Wednesday on the final afternoon while the Rams had just needed to avoid defeat to secure a top-six finish, only to go down 3-0 at home to lowly Reading.

We can only hope 1 May 2027 provides us with half as much drama on the final day of the regular season.

Three points separated the top five teams in the Championship after 15 games in 2014-15

With eight play-off places now up for grabs, the odds are it might even exceed it.

And we can all take heart from the fact the table now is slightly tighter than the one in 2014-15 was after 15 games, while it's worth noting that only one of those top five fell away in the run-in.

Does that suggest our three promoted sides will come from the current top five?

The Championship's top goalscorer Will Lankshear has netted 13 of the 532 goals across 180 games in the division so far this season

If you want lots of goals and a tense battle at the top, then look no further than the Championship.

No other league in Europe is as tightly contested right now.

The Dutch Eredivisie comes closest with three points separating the top five, compared to just one point in the Championship.

However, the season is only nine games old in the Netherlands, as opposed to 15 in the English second tier.

Only two points separate the top four in the Belgian Pro League after 11 matches but there is a nine-point gap from first to fifth.

And it is not just the promotion race delivering so far this season - the entire division is coming up with the goods in terms of entertainment.

The last time goals were banged in at a higher rate in the second tier, England were about to win the World Cup for the first and only time to date.

This season's ratio of 2.96 goals per game is the highest in the 60 years since there were 3.08 per game across the 1965-66 campaign.

With 532 goals already netted in the Championship, we are on course for a total of 1,633 should the trend continue.

That would be the highest number of goals achieved at this level since 1957-58 when there were 1,637.

The highest number of goals ever in the second tier was in 1926-27, when there were 22 teams in the division and fewer games played overall (462) compared to today (552).

Third-placed Stoke City have only been given a 5.26% chance of automatic promotion by Opta (data correct as of 19 November)

Predicting the completely unpredictable might be a futile task, particularly this season.

But Opta's Supercomputer has tried to do just that by crunching the numbers to estimate the likely outcome of every remaining match using its power rankings tool and betting odds.

Opta's model considers the strength of opponents and simulates the remaining fixtures thousands of times.

The results? Middlesbrough will win the title with Wolves gaining the second automatic promotion spot.

Birmingham, Stoke, West Brom and Southampton are predicted to finish in the play-offs, as are Swansea , though they will have to do so without boss Vitor Matos who has left for French Ligue 1 club Strasbourg , while Opta expect West Ham to replace QPR in the top eight.

Woodman believes Parker's experience will help the Hammers recover from their recent blip, which prompted the club to sack boss Nuno Espirito Santo and replace him with their former midfielder.

"He knows this league inside out," said Woodman. "I'd be hard pressed to say who's better equipped for getting teams out of this league than Scotty Parker.

"He's a phenomenal manager and I think he'll do really well at West Ham."

McAnuff believes Middlesbrough are the ones to beat.

"I love what Kim Helberg's done," he said. "They've missed Will Lankshear the past couple of games, but I still have them as my favourites. I think anyone who's above them this year will be getting automatically promoted."

Four of the teams currently in the race will meet in the first game after the international break when Stoke host Birmingham and West Brom visit Swansea.

"One of those, maybe two, will really look at it and go: 'Why can't we be the Coventry this season?'" added McAnuff.

"There's no reason why Birmingham - with such an open start to the league, particularly going down to eight teams this year - can't at least get into the play-offs.

"They will have designs on staying higher, I'm sure of that, but I do think some of the bigger teams are going to come good later on in the season."

MN202611_158eevtfliv.t:
Amakimbirane areba Olivier Nsiabamfumu, ukorana na kompanyi Ya’ats Sports, na Aurélien Logeais, ufite aho ahuriye na Ventilo Sports, ku mafaranga ya komisiyo ashobora kugera kuri miliyoni z’amayero.

Ku wa 30 Kamena 2025, RDC na FC Barcelone byashyize umukono ku masezerano y’ubufatanye mu kwamamaza igihugu, afite agaciro ka miliyoni 43 z’amayero, azishyurwa mu gihe cy’imyaka ine.

Aya masezerano yari agamije kumenyekanisha Congo nk’ahantu nyaburanga, ubukerarugendo n’ishoramari, hifashishijwe izina n’ubwamamare by’ikipe ya FC Barcelone.

Mu byo RDC yagombaga kubona harimo gushyira ikirango “R.D. Congo, cœur de l’Afrique” ku myambaro yo kwishyushya y’abakinnyi, kwamamaza igihugu ku mbuga n’ibikoresho bya FC Barcelone, kumenyekanisha RDC mu bikorwa by’ubucuruzi n’itangazamakuru bya Barça, ndetse no gushyiraho ahantu hazajya hamenyekanisha Congo muri sitade yayo.

Aya masezerano kandi yari akubiyemo gahunda zijyanye n’iterambere ry’umupira w’amaguru, zirimo amahugurwa n’ibikorwa bya Barça Academy.

Yari mu rwego rwa gahunda ya RDC yo gukoresha siporo mu kwamamaza igihugu no kongera ijambo ryacyo ku rwego mpuzamahanga. Muri rusange, RDC yagombaga kwishyura hagati ya miliyoni 10 na 11.5 z’amayero buri mwaka.

Olivier Nsiabamfumu avuga ko ari we wazanye umushinga

Olivier Nsiabamfumu, wahoze ari umukinnyi w’umupira w’amaguru, akaba akorana na Ya’ats Sports, avuga ko ari we watangije ibiganiro by’ubufatanye hagati ya RDC na FC Barcelone.

Amakuru yatangajwe avuga ko yatangiye gukora kuri uwo mushinga kuva mu 2023, kandi ko FC Barcelone yamwemeye nk’umuhuza wayo mu ibaruwa yo ku wa 24 Mutarama 2025, Perezida w’iyi kipe Joan Laporta yandikiye Perezida wa RDC Félix Tshisekedi.

Mu ibaruwa bivugwa ko yanditswe icyo gihe, Nsiabamfumu yagaragajwe nk’umuhuza mu masezerano ndetse n’uwagize igitekerezo cyo kuyashyiraho.

Abamwunganira bavuga ko Ya’ats Sports ari yo yagize uruhare rukomeye mu kubaka no kugera kuri ayo masezerano, bityo ikaba ikwiye guhabwa komisiyo ijyanye n’akazi yakoze.

Aurélien Logeais na Ventilo Sports binjiye mu masezerano

Mu gihe ibiganiro byari bimaze igihe bikorwa, Aurélien Logeais, ufitanye isano na Ventilo Sports, na we yaje kwinjira muri uyu mushinga.

Bivugwa ko ku wa 13 Gicurasi 2025, Minisitiri wa Siporo wa RDC, Didier Budimbu Ntubuanga, yashyize umukono ku nyandiko iha Ventilo Sports inshingano zo gufasha guhuza inzego zitandukanye kugira ngo ubufatanye na FC Barcelone bugerweho.

Iyi nyandiko ni yo yabaye intandaro y’amakimbirane, kuko Olivier Nsiabamfumu yari asanzwe akora kuri uwo mushinga mbere y’uko Logeais na Ventilo Sports bahabwa izindi nshingano.

Ventilo Sports yo ivuga ko na yo yakoze akazi kayo mu gufasha guhuza impande zombi, kandi ko ifite uburenganzira bwo guhabwa amafaranga ajyanye n’akazi yakoze.

Imwe mu ngingo zikomeye zateje amakimbirane ni amafaranga ya komisiyo yagombaga guhabwa abahuza.

Amakuru ya Mediapart avuga ko Ventilo Sports yari yarahawe komisiyo ingana na 10% by’agaciro k’amasezerano, ikaba yari hafi miliyoni 4.3 z’amayero.

Ibi byateje ikibazo kuko Ya’ats Sports na Olivier Nsiabamfumu na bo bavuga ko ari bo bakwiye guhabwa komisiyo, bitewe n’uko bari bamaze igihe bakora kuri uwo mushinga.

Iyi komisiyo ya miliyoni 4.3 z’amayero ni yo ivugwa mu nyandiko ya Mediapart. Imibare n’imiterere y’amafaranga abahuza basabwa biratandukanye mu zindi nkuru, bityo ntibigomba gufatwa nk’amafaranga yamaze kwishyurwa.

FC Barcelone ntikozwa ibyo kwishyura kompanyi zirenze imwe

Mu biganiro byabaye mbere y’uko amasezerano asinywa, FC Barcelone bivugwa ko yari ifite impungenge ku buryo komisiyo yari kugabanywa hagati y’abahuza.

Cesar Martinez Fontana, umwe mu bantu bakorana na Perezida wa Barça, bivugwa ko yandikiye Minisitiri Didier Budimbu ku wa 28 Kamena 2025, amwibutsa ko Ya’ats Sports ari yo yari yatangiye gukora kuri uwo mushinga mbere y’abandi.

Mu biganiro byakurikiyeho, Barça yagerageje gushaka uburyo ikibazo cyakemuka, harimo igitekerezo cyo kugabanya komisiyo imwe ikagabanywa hagati y’abahuza.

Ariko ibyo ntibyahise bikemura ikibazo, kuko impande zari zifite ibyo zishyize imbere zitari zimwe.

Aurélien Logeais na Ventilo Sports bahakana ko binjiye mu masezerano mu buryo butemewe cyangwa ko bagiye kwigabiza amafaranga atari ayabo.

Ababunganira bavuga ko bafite ibimenyetso byerekana ko Ventilo Sports yakoze akazi yari yasabwe, kandi ko komisiyo yayo yari izwi, iteganyijwe kandi igomba kwishyurwa na FC Barcelone, aho kuba Guverinoma ya RDC.

Banahakana ibirego bavuga ko bishobora kwangiza izina ry’umukiriya wabo, bakavuga ko nta nyungu y’amafaranga yagenewe umukozi wa Leta ya Congo yari muri iyo gahunda.

Minisitiri Didier Budimbu na we asobanura uruhare rwa Ventilo Sports

Minisitiri wa Siporo wa RDC, Didier Budimbu, yavuze ko Ventilo Sports yari ifite uruhare mu gufasha guhuza ikipe n’ubuyobozi bwa minisiteri, kugira ngo ibiganiro bitangire kandi ubufatanye bushoboke.

Ariko ibibazo byakomeje kwibazwa ku mpamvu Ventilo Sports yahawe izo nshingano mu gihe Ya’ats Sports yari imaze igihe ikora kuri uwo mushinga.

Minisitiri yanavuze ko RDC itagomba kugira uruhare mu gukemura amakimbirane y’abahuza cyangwa mu micungire y’imibanire yabo na FC Barcelone, nubwo amakuru y’iperereza avuga ko yagize uruhare mu biganiro byerekeye komisiyo.

Amakimbirane hagati y’abahuza yaje kugira ingaruka ku masezerano ubwayo, aho ubufatanye bwahagaritswe by’agateganyo mu gihe impande zitandukanye zari zitarumvikana ku kibazo cy’amafaranga.

Mu ntangiriro za shampiyona ya 2026–2027, ikirango “ R.D. Congo, cœur de l’Afrique ” cyaje kubura ku myambaro yo kwishyushya y’abakinnyi ba FC Barcelone, ibintu byatumye abantu bibaza niba ubufatanye bwaba bwahagaze.

Amakuru yatangajwe avuga ko RDC yari yarahagaritse by’agateganyo kwishyura amafaranga agera kuri miliyoni 10.5 z’amayero yari agenewe umwaka wa kabiri w’amasezerano, mu rwego rwo gushaka ko ikibazo cy’abahuza gikemuka.

Nubwo ikirango cyaje kongera kugaragara ku bindi bikoresho byo kwamamaza, ikibazo cy’amafaranga n’abahuza cyakomeje guteza impaka.

Ikibazo cy’amafaranga ya komisiyo cyaje no kugera mu nkiko zo mu Bufaransa.

Ya’ats Sports, ihagarariwe na Olivier Nsiabamfumu, yareze Ventilo Sports, isaba ko yishyurwa cyangwa ihabwa indishyi kubera ibyo ivuga ko yakoze kuri uyu mushinga, ariko undi muhuza akaza kwinjira mu masezerano akayigizayo.

Ventilo Sports na Aurélien Logeais na bo bahakana ibyo bashinjwa, bakavuga ko bakoze akazi kabo kandi ko bafite uburenganzira ku mafaranga yateganyijwe.

Iyi ntambara y’amategeko yerekana ko ikibazo kitakiri ugushaka komisiyo gusa, ahubwo cyahindutse ikibazo cyo kumenya uwagize uruhare nyakuri mu kuzana amasezerano, uwari ufite uburenganzira bwo kuyahuza, n’uwari ukwiye guhabwa amafaranga.

Aya masezerano ntabwo yari umushinga wo kwamamaza gusa. RDC yari iri mu mugambi wo gukoresha siporo mu kongera kumenyekana no kwigaragaza ku rwego mpuzamahanga, cyane cyane mu gihe yari ifite amakimbirane n’u Rwanda ajyanye n’umutekano mu burasirazuba bwa Congo.

Perezida Félix Tshisekedi yari ashyigikiye gahunda yo gukoresha siporo mu kumenyekanisha igihugu, mu gihe RDC yashakaga kugera ku bafana b’umupira w’amaguru ku isi binyuze mu makipe akomeye yo mu Burayi.

Amasezerano na FC Barcelone yari umwe mu mishinga minini muri gahunda yo gukoresha amakipe akomeye mu kwamamaza igihugu, nyuma y’ubundi bufatanye na AS Monaco na AC Milan.

MN202611_8z4wj00vwq.t:
Darragh MacAnthony marked 20 years as Peterborough chairman earlier this year

Darragh MacAnthony says he is "working around the clock" to protect his "legacy" as Peterborough United chairman, with the club facing another fight to retain their League One status.

Posh's hierarchy had targeted promotion in 2026-27, but are 22nd in the third-tier, having finished 18th in the past two seasons.

Peterborough sacked manager Luke Williams after 11 months in charge in September and appointed Robbie Savage, but they are on a run of no win in seven in all competition.

Last month, MacAnthony "promised" to sell his 75% stake in the club after 20 years as chairman if they had not reached League One's top 10 by February.

On Tuesday, MacAnthony issued a lengthy statement on the club's website , external in which he said he "would not outstay my welcome at this amazing club".

"If we don't turn things around, I will look to put the club in the hands of someone who can do a better job than me, because that is the right thing to do," the statement added.

"It is not something I want to do or need to do, but if it is right for our club, it will get done. You have my word on that."

MacAnthony sold half his stake to Jason Neale and Stewart Thompson in 2018, through their Canadian business Kelgary Sports and Entertainment, but became sole majority shareholder again five years later after they stood down from the board.

"I am working around the clock to make sure my legacy as owner will not be defined by this season," MacAnthony said.

"I have been in this game long enough to know there will be more downs before the highs return, but I have staked my ownership on the highs returning.

"I have done that because, as always, I am an eternal optimist, and I honestly believe our club, our players and our staff will turn this awful time around for you, our fans."

Fiona Harvey appeared on Piers Morgan Uncensored in 2024, after the release of Netflix's Baby Reindeer

A woman who allegedly inspired the stalker character Martha in the hit Netflix drama Baby Reindeer is to appear at Harrow Crown Court on charges of racially aggravated harassment without violence.

Fiona Harvey, 61, is accused of with sending several emails and three voicemails including antisemitic material to lawyer Mark Lewis, between 4 September and 9 October 2025.

During a hearing at Highbury Corner Magistrates' Court on Thursday, the court heard that Mr Lewis initially believed Harvey was a potential client.

Harvey of Camden, North London, did not indicate a plea, but elected for a Crown Court trial.

The charge is an either-way offence, which means it can be heard in either a magistrates' court or Crown Court.

She will next appear at Harrow Crown Court for a pre-trial preparation hearing on 17 December.

Harvey has previously identified herself as the woman on whom Martha is based, after the release of Richard Gadd's Emmy Award-winning series in 2024.

She is suing the streamer £128m for defamation, negligence and privacy violations, arguing that that Netflix told "brutal lies" about her to over 50 million viewers around the world.

Netflix denies the claim, which will be heard in front of a jury on May 18, 2027, at the US District Court for the Central District of California.

MN202611_11o640xz0hr.t:
A bar-tailed godwit similar to Phil being fitted with a tracking device

A bird named Phil has astonished conservationists by completing a 6,800-mile (10,900km) round trip from England's east coast to Siberia and back.

Bar-tailed godwits are champion fliers, migrating between Britain and the Arctic, but the precise routes used by individual birds is largely unknown.

Phil was fitted with a tiny solar-powered tracker that recorded his movements throughout the journey.

The data showed he travelled from The Wash , external to the Wadden Sea, along the coasts of the Netherlands, Germany and Denmark, before continuing to Siberia.

On his return, he crossed the Arctic Ocean to northern Norway, stopping on three islands before heading back through the Wadden Sea to The Wash.

Bar-tailed godwits resting on the beach in the Wadden Sea

Scientists say Phil's extraordinary travels highlight the importance of protecting the world's wetlands, which are havens for millions of migratory birds each year.

Dr Nigel Clark, of the conservation charity, The Wash Wader Research Group, said The Wash is the UK's single most important coastal wetland for migratory waders, with spectacular numbers seen in autumn and winter.

"Tracking birds like Phil the Godwit shows us how connected the Wash is with the rest of the flyway," he said.

Jeff Kew, RSPB Coastal Advisor, said many migratory bird species cross borders, depending on a whole network of wetlands along the way.

That's why it's so important to look after these special places."

Bar-tailed godwits are wading birds of similar size to pigeons, but with long bills and legs.

They are regarded as one of nature's long-distance endurance athletes, with one subspecies making the longest known non-stop migration of any bird, flying 8,425 miles (13,559km) from Alaska to New Zealand.

Phil's journey included a handful of stops to rest and refuel.

He will now spend the winter relaxing with thousands of other wading birds at the Snettisham Nature Reserve in Norfolk.

MN202611_kr769m02qg.t:
Pete Hegseth met Venezuela's interim president at the presidential palace

The United States and Venezuela have re-established military ties less than a year after US forces seized the then-leader of the South American country, Nicolás Maduro, in a raid on the capital, Caracas.

The interim government led by Delcy Rodríguez, Maduro's former vice-president, signed a military co-operation agreement with US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth on Wednesday.

Few details about the deal have been released so far but Hegseth said that Venezuela had "gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner" in less than 12 months.

Interim President Rodríguez said the deal would help confront "common threats".

Military co-operation between the two countries was terminated in 2005 by Hugo Chávez, Venezuela's left-wing president at the time.

Chávez alleged that US military personnel sent to Venezuela to train their counterparts had made disparaging remarks about his government.

He also accused the US military office located in Fuerte Tiuna, Venezuela's largest military complex, of being "an organ of the CIA... conspiring against the government".

Under Nicolás Maduro, who succeeded Chávez after the latter's death from cancer, relations between the two countries deteriorated further.

They reached rock bottom late last year when the US doubled its reward for information leading to Maduro's capture to $50m (£38m) and eventually seized him on 3 January in a military raid.

Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, are now in custody in New York on charges of drug-trafficking and conspiracy to commit torture , which they deny.

Hegseth addressed the change in the two countries' relationship since Maduro was seized in his speech at the US embassy in Caracas on Wednesday.

"It's a great honour to be here as the first United States Secretary of War this century to set foot in Venezuela. The weight of this moment does not escape me," he said.

"Just one year ago, my presence here, our presence here would have been deemed impossible, almost unimaginable," he added before recalling a public appearance by then-President Maduro which had angered the Trump administration.

"Exactly one year ago today, the indicted narco-terrorist fugitive Nicolás Maduro, the man who spent more than a decade handing Venezuela's borders and territory to terrorists from all over the world, stood on a stage, not too far from here, and yelled mockingly: 'Come and get me!'. Well, we answered that call."

Hegseth added that the result of the US military raid on 3 January had been as Maduro predicted, quoting the deposed leader's words: "No war, yes peace."

He described the deal signed by him and Venezuela's defence minister on Wednesday as a "new chapter for the United States, for Venezuela, for the Venezuelan military and for the Western Hemisphere through the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition".

Rodríguez described it as "extraordinarily relevant for our bilateral relations".

"In a matter of months, secretary, we have turned very difficult moments for our people into a space for co-operation and mutual benefit for both of our countries," she said addressing Hegseth during a meeting at the presidential palace.

While no details of the deal have been published, in her speech Rodríguez mentioned the training of Venezuela's armed forces and improving its "operational equipment" and access to new technology "to confront shared threats".

In his speech at the US embassy, Hegseth was more direct about who he considers to be those threats. Addressing "the narco-terrorists who abuse this [Venezuela] as a safe haven", he warned that "we will hunt you down, we will find you, and we will kill you".

From Venezuela, Hegseth travelled on to neighbouring Colombia, whose president, Abelardo de la Espriella, is a close ally of the Trump administration.

Colombia is already part of the US-led Americas Counter Cartel Coalition and in August, Hegseth had floated the possibility of joint US-Colombian military operations against armed groups.

On Wednesday, President de la Espriella took to X to deny a report by the New York Times which had stated that he had rejected carrying out joint operations , external .

In his post, he stressed that any decision would be taken while respecting Colombia's constitution, and the country's laws and sovereignty.

Hegseth reposted the tweet commenting that the US-Colombian partnership "is stronger than ever before".
