MN202611_cpaagea6j0.t:
The 8th Eastern African Research and Innovation Management Association (EARIMA) concluded on November 19.

KIGALI – Like many African countries, Rwanda has invested in research centers, innovation hubs and funding programs intended to turn scientific ideas into products, technologies and solutions for its development needs.

However, in most cases, ensuring that research produces results that people, businesses and public institutions can actually use, remains untenable beyond just generating knowledge.

A biomedical innovation that never reaches a hospital, or an agricultural solution that never gets to farmers, remains an unfinished achievement.

Rwanda’s first Innovation Survey, covering 2022 to 2024, found that 89 per cent of higher education institutions were actively engaged in innovation, while 86.1 per cent had introduced new innovations during the period.

However, only 52.8 per cent had dedicated budgets for innovation activities. These figures point to an ecosystem generating ideas, but where the resources needed to develop and sustain them are not yet widespread.

The National Research and Innovation Fund has invested nearly Rwf8 billion in 126 projects across areas including health, agriculture, energy, local production and digital services. More than 20 of the projects have been identified as having commercialization potential.

The National Council for Science and Technology has also been working with the University of Rwanda to attract private-sector investment and connect academic research with market needs.

Experts across the continent say that research in health systems too often produces publications and pilot projects without changing how services are delivered.

In Kigali, Prof. Nahya Salim, the Director of Research, Publication and Innovation at Tanzania’s Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences, told members of the 8th Eastern African Research and Innovation Management Association (EARIMA) that this trend has to change.

“An intervention may demonstrate strong results under controlled clinical conditions but perform very differently when introduced into a real health system with limited staff, resources and infrastructure,” Nahya explained.

Research therefore needs to examine not only whether an intervention works, but whether hospitals and communities can realistically use it.

Prof. Nahya Salim, the Director of Research, Publication and Innovation at Tanzania’s Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences.

She also warned that promising programs can disappear when donor funding runs out because governments were not involved early enough to incorporate them into national budgets.

“When the program fades out or ends, we have not initiated to our leaders where the program was implemented to create a budget line. This is needed for our technology and innovations to survive,” she noted.

Beyond healthcare, Prof. Eli Katunguka, Vice Chancellor of Uganda’s Kyambogo University and chairman EARIMA, argued that African countries must become better at converting their research and resources into economic value rather than continuing to export raw materials.

He said research institutions need strong management systems, sustainable investment and partnerships that connect scientific work to industry and public needs.

Research managers, he suggested, should be recognized as strategic professionals who help secure funding, manage partnerships, protect intellectual property and guide innovations towards practical application.

Prof. Eli Katunguka, Vice Chancellor of Uganda’s Kyambogo University and chairman EARIMA speaking at the confrence.

The University of Rwanda has established specialized centers in areas such as data science, energy, biodiversity and biomedical engineering, while its innovation hubs are intended to help researchers develop and test solutions with commercial potential.

In January 2026, the African Development Bank approved $29.85 million in financing for the second phase of Rwanda’s Centre of Excellence for Biomedical Engineering and e-Health, aimed at expanding training, research facilities and links with the private sector.

Prof. Abraham Haileamlak Mitike, Principal of the University of Rwanda’s College of Medicine and Health Sciences, said universities must become partners in entrepreneurship, innovation and national development.

“The university of the 20th century can no longer be viewed solely as a place for teaching and academic inquiry. It must become a driver of innovation ecosystems, a catalyst for entrepreneurship, a trusted policy advisor, and a strategic partner in national development,” he emphasized.

Prof. Abraham Haileamlak Mitike, Principal of the University of Rwanda’s College of Medicine and Health Sciences.

Rwanda’s own revised science and technology strategy acknowledges that translating research into scalable solutions, evidence-based decisions and measurable development outcomes remains limited.

It calls for stronger pathways to move ideas from research and prototypes towards adoption and wider use.

Held under the theme Advancing research and innovation management for African socio-economic transformation, the three-day EARIMA conference which concluded on November 19, brought together researchers and research managers to examine how institutions can create a difference.

MN202611_lwdntl6kaf.t:
The US is playing catch-up with China's dominance in critical minerals mining and processing across Africa (file photo)

A US-led consortium, Frontier Minerals, has won the tender to develop Kenya's Mrima Hill mining project, beating seven bidders, including companies from China and Australia.

The site is estimated to hold deposits of critical minerals worth more than $60bn (£45bn), including niobium, used in electric vehicles, aerospace and defence technology.

Frontier Minerals says its proposal aims to keep more of the economic benefits in Kenya through "processing and refining of minerals in-country".

The deal comes as Washington seeks greater access to Africa's minerals, aiming to strengthen US supply chains and compete with China.

Frontier Minerals brings together three US companies - Bunker Hill Mining Corp, American Resources Corporation and ReElement Technologies Corporation. The consortium combines expertise in mineral resource development, critical materials supply chains and advanced refining technologies.

A central part of its proposal is to develop mineral processing and refining capacity in Kenya. Brad Marnett from Frontier Minerals said the company wanted the country to capture more value from its mineral resources.

Mrima Hill is located in Kwale County, near Kenya's Indian Ocean coastline. The site covers about 390 acres of forest.

The prospect of mining in the area has raised concerns among local residents, who fear the project could damage the forest and threaten their ancestral heritage.

There are also questions over whether communities living near the site will benefit from the investment.

Marnett was keen to reassure Kenyans that they would benefit: "We intend to create lasting opportunities for Kenyan workers, businesses and the wider economy through capacity-building and targeted investment, while prioritising environmental management and performance."

The consortium must still obtain a prospecting licence and meet the necessary regulatory requirements before the project can proceed.

The tender decision has drawn objections from competing bidders.

Reuters news agency reports that two rival companies intend to challenge the selection, with Australia's RareX alleging that Frontier Minerals missed an earlier submission deadline.

Kenya's government has maintained that the process was open and transparent.

The project comes as US strives to secure alternative sources of critical minerals and reduce dependence on China, which dominates the processing of several key minerals.

Washington has been pursuing partnerships with mineral-rich African countries, including the Democratic Republic of Congo and Zambia, as it seeks to strengthen supply chains for industries ranging from electric vehicles to defence technology.

Kenya's mining ministry says the sector is an important part of its plans to diversify the economy beyond traditional sources of revenue such as tourism, agriculture and financial services.

MN202611_oti9lgb62a.t:
The Welsh government said recent investment was starting to have an impact

Wales' health minister has insisted that the NHS in Wales is in its strongest position heading into winter than ever before.

Mabon ap Gwynfor was speaking after the latest NHS performance figures showed that more than 11,500 people waited 12 hours or more in emergency departments from arrival until admission, transfer or discharge in one month.

In September, there were 4,900 patient pathways waiting more than two years for planned treatment - a fall of 160 compared to the previous month.

But the overall number of people waiting for NHS treatment in Wales has risen for the sixth month in a row. In September, there were 721,400 waiting for planned treatment, compared to 714,200 in August.

'I spent more than two days waiting in A&E' - NHS bids to end corridor care

My 93-year-old mother waited 10 hours on the floor for an ambulance

With the longest waits falling slightly, ap Gwynfor said the figures were a sign that an investment of £145m earlier this year was starting to lead to improvements.

Earlier this week, Plaid Cymru ministers announced an extra £500m to cut waiting lists.

The latest figures on A&E performance showed that, in October, nearly two-thirds (61.1%) of patients spent less than four hours in emergency departments from arrival until admission, transfer or discharge. 11,830 patients waited 12 hours or more, though the way those figures are recorded has changed in recent weeks.

There was a decrease in the number of patient pathways when it comes to diagnostics, falling to just under 110,900, but an increase in the number of cases waiting for therapy, rising to just under 66,500.

Speaking to BBC Wales during a visit to Llandough Hospital on Thursday, ap Gwynfor said: "We are starting to see signs of improvement and it is encouraging we're on the right track, but we are yet to see the investment's full impact.

"The NHS is in a stronger position now than it's ever been in preparation for the winter."

But he warned of "impacts beyond our control", such as the El Niño climate phenomenon , or a flu pandemic, adding: "We are as prepared as can be, and I'm confident that the health boards have worked with us to develop the best plans."

Mabon ap Gwynfor says the government has a plan to cut waiting lists

"The situation as it is in emergency care in many departments across Wales isn't what it should be, and we need to fix that," ap Gwynfor added.

"We need to make sure that people don't wait too long, either in an ambulance, in an ED, or in a corridor, or waiting for discharge.

"That's why we've got a plan to increase and improve that flow to get people out."

Prof Jon Barry, director for Wales at the Royal College of Surgeons of England said it was "disappointing" to see waiting lists increase, "especially as we head towards the depths of winter".

"Thousands of patients are still waiting more than two years for treatment, many living with pain, restricted mobility, and worsening health," he said.

"We welcome the £500 million in additional funding for NHS Wales, including £25 million to build and expand surgical hubs, announced in the draft Budget this week.

Ireland captain Dan Sheehan has been named at number eight for Saturday's highly anticipated Nations Championship match against world champions South Africa in Dublin.

Having won all 42 of his previous caps at hooker, the 28-year-old returns after recovering from a concussion to partner flankers Ryan Baird and Josh van der Flier in the back row.

Ireland head coach Andy Farrell has faced an injury crisis at number eight with regular skipper Caelan Doris, Jack Conan, Sean Jansen and recent debutant James McNabney all ruled out.

Nick Timoney, who was handed the jersey for last week's victory over Fiji, drops to the bench.

With Doris and Conan unavailable, Sheehan anchored the scrum in Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster last month, but Saturday will be his first Test run-out in the back row.

Sheehan's move means that Ronan Kelleher keeps his place at hooker after starting the Fiji game, again joining props Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong in the front row.

After being rested last week, Joe McCarthy returns to the second row to partner Tadhg Beirne, with Van der Flier edging out Timoney for the number seven jersey.

Sam Prendergast starts at fly-half after being cleared to face the Springboks on Wednesday, with Jamison Gibson-Park retained at scrum-half.

Prendergast, 23, was cited for his hip-drop tackle on Fiji's Peceli Yato - which was not punished on the pitch - but an independent disciplinary panel ruled the challenge was not worthy of a red card.

Robbie Henshaw and Stuart McCloskey both return to midfield after Farrell opted to pair Jamie Osborne and Bundee Aki in a new-look centre partnership against Fiji.

However, Osborne was replaced by McCloskey in the third minute after sustaining a pectoral injury that has ruled him out of the South Africa game, while Aki drops to the bench.

With Hugo Keenan returning to full-back for his 50th cap after sitting out the Fiji game, Mack Hansen switches to the left wing with Robert Baloucoune retained on the right. Tommy O'Brien, who scored two tries from the left wing against Fiji, drops out of the squad.

Farrell has opted for a split of five forwards and three backs on the bench. Tom Stewart, Tom O'Toole, Sam Illo, James Ryan and Timoney provide pack cover with Craig Casey, Ciaran Frawley and Aki named as backline reinforcements.

Nick Timoney (left) drops to the bench while Sam Prendergast (right) starts at fly-half after being cleared of foul play

South Africa, who named their team on Monday, make five changes with record cap holder Eben Etzebeth recalled to the second row.

Cameron Hanekom is named at number eight, replacing Jasper Wiese, who was handed a four-week suspension after being sent off for a dangerous clear-out in last week's defeat by France.

Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw are named as the starting front row.

Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus also named Nche, Marx and Louw to start the France game but swapped them out for Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit shortly before kick-off at the Stade de France.

Erasmus is not permitted to attend the Aviva Stadium encounter after being handed a six-match ban by World Rugby for questioning the integrity of the match officials in his team's loss to Les Bleus.

The 54-year-old has since announced he will be hosting an online watchalong of the match while he watches from his team's Dublin hotel.

South Africa sit second in the Nations Championship southern hemisphere standings, a point adrift of New Zealand.

A South Africa win over Ireland coupled with England beating the All Blacks (Saturday, 14:10 GMT) would be enough for Erasmus' side to seal a place in the 29 November final against the top-ranked northern hemisphere side at Twickenham.

Ireland must beat the Springboks and hope France and England falter against Argentina and New Zealand to finish top.

The Springboks won 24-13 at Aviva Stadium last year, their first victory over Ireland in Dublin since 2012.

Baroness Heather Hallett chairs UK Covid-19 Inquiry - this is her seventh report

The UK should co-ordinate its response to any future pandemic with the Republic of Ireland because of the added complexity of disease control across the open Irish border, the Covid-19 inquiry has said.

In its latest 'Test, trace and isolate' report into the programme of test and trace, it said cooperation was needed "to ensure that border control measures are effective and operable in practice".

During the pandemic, Northern Ireland chose to align its international border control measures with the UK rather than with the Republic.

Inquiry chair Dame Heather Hallett said that despite this decision, there was close liaison between the UK government, devolved administrations and the Irish government.

Northern Ireland developed its own contact tracing app

In addition, in May 2020 the Northern Ireland Executive announced it would develop its own contact tracing app rather than adopt the one in development in England.

It used the same technology and provider as the Republic of Ireland and the cross border apps were the "first in the world to achieve interoperability", the report said.

"The Northern Ireland Executive entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Irish government on 7 April 2020 to allow regular data-sharing and the sharing of information on international travel policies," said the inquiry report.

This included weekly meetings between the two governments' health departments and the sharing of data in relation to the trajectory of the pandemic and information about international travel policy.

It also involved working closely together in order to inform policies about border control.

"The complexity of relations between the four nations, together with the additional complexity arising from the land border between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland, must be carefully examined and addressed in the development of any future border control approach."

Both sides of the Irish border were left open to potential infection risk because of the lower level of measures put in place by the UK, report said

The report also said both sides of the Irish border were left open to potential infection risk because of the lower level of measures put in place by the UK government.

"By April 2020, 93% of countries and territories had put measures in place – such as flight suspensions, border closures and travel restrictions – to control their international borders," said the report.

By contrast, it said, the UK government only requested (rather than directed) travellers from Wuhan, China, to self-isolate in January 2020 and travellers from some other high-risk areas to self-isolate in February 2020.

"This did not prevent a coachload of tourists from Wuhan entering the UK and travelling from England to Scotland and then to Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland in February 2020.

"The UK government implemented no further border control measures until June 2020."

Only 78 tracers were trained by May 2020

The inquiry found that the test and trace system was in part successful in Northern Ireland.

Despite having only 78 tracers trained by May 2020, the programme worked effectively because it operated from a centralised office.

"The team adopted a specific strategy that emphasised being personable and convivial in their interactions.

"By June 2020, 92% of people who had tested positive for Covid-19 and those who had been in close contact with them were reached within 24 hours," said the report.

It said the centralised system worked in Northern Ireland because its population is relatively small and it has a single, comparatively small healthcare system that enabled flexibility and a more rapid response.

"The scale of its system meant that it was able to replicate some of the advantages typically associated with local teams."

The inquiry report also found Northern Ireland was successful in the operation of payment entitlements to people self-isolating because it differed from other parts of the UK in using an existing Discretionary Support scheme.

On a UK-wide basis, Dame Hallett said failings in testing and tracing left the UK "effectively blind" to how quickly Covid was spreading early in the pandemic.

"The UK was simply not prepared. Too many lives were cut short," she said.

Campaign group Covid-19 Bereaved Families for Justice UK said the inquiry has "exposed the lies and incompetence that left thousands of us grieving loved ones who should still be here".

The group said the government failures, such as the slow testing rate and sidelining of local public health teams "cost lives".

MN202611_15pylzmqje8.t:
Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United head coach will be at Liverpool on 22 November

"We have to find a way to create the best habits and culture that makes us close to winning every single game."

Mauricio Pochettino has used his first interview as Manchester United head coach to outline his vision for the club.

The former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea boss wasted no time getting across the Atlantic Ocean after completing his stint in charge of the United States on Tuesday.

He met key staff on Wednesday, took training for the first time on Thursday and conducts his first wider media conference at United's Carrington training ground on Friday.

The 54-year-old is facing a packed schedule, starting with a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

Pochettino accepted a big challenge. United are 18th in the table. By 17:00 GMT on Saturday, they could be bottom.

So, what are the Argentine's priorities as he begins the task of trying to transform United's season?

"To create the culture is the most important [thing]," he told United's in-house media in a 15-minute introductory chat.

Manchester won't always be blue - Pochettino

Fitness obsessed & 'control freak' - what can Man Utd expect from Pochettino?

Matheus Cunha's injury-time goal against Roma on 3 November sealed one of only three Manchester United victories in 15 games this season

It would be easy to point to areas of the pitch where United have been deficient this season. However, it cannot be totally dismissed that virtually the same group of players were transformed over the second half of last season by the recently sacked Michael Carrick, who guided them to third in the Premier League and Champions League qualification.

Remarkably, Pochettino has won twice as many matches in charge of the USA this season than the three victories United have managed, with a 100% record from six games.

United, by contrast, have not won in the Premier League since August, while two of their three victories have required the Red Devils to come from behind. Their single clean sheet came against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.

One of the most immediate tasks for Pochettino will be to alter the mindset of players who seem to have become restricted by the pressure they have found themselves subjected to.

"It is a mistake to see the situation," he said. "We need to see the potential of this club.

"We need to understand it is a game, and to connect with the game we need to feel free. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is our priority now; to work with them and take the pressure.

"Pressure needs to bring energy. Responsibility needs to bring energy because if not, it is too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back."

Diogo Dalot is consoled by Manchester United team-mate Joshua Zirkzee after being substituted during the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa

That said, there are some glaring issues that Carrick was unable to fix and Pochettino must find an answer to. The most obvious is defence.

Who should the cornerstones of United's defence be?

The Carrick regime felt Leny Yoro was the player with the attributes - pace, strength and control - most suited to their needs. Yet, at 21, Yoro is prone to mistakes and he has also been needed at right-back because regular right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have, at times, been required on the left.

Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt have not been reliable fitness wise. Pochettino knows the baggage attached to Martinez, given his post-match criticisms of the club hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid, and the knowledge his fellow countryman's contract expires in the summer.

Harry Maguire has started all 10 league games this season but suffered a back spasm in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, immediately before the international break, and had to be replaced at half-time. Maguire has many attributes, but his presence does restrict the ability to press high up the field.

Ayden Heaven has made eight appearances in all competitions but has previously been regarded as being behind Yoro in terms of his overall development.

The 27-year-old was consoled by Joshua Zirkzee when he was replaced against Villa, such was the negative fan reaction to his performance, which included conceding a penalty at the start of the second-half.

It can justifiably be argued if Dalot has the talent to match the 260 club appearances he has now made.

However, for his faults, coaches love his attitude.

Dalot has been described to BBC Sport as having one of the most committed and professional approaches to the game, that he is someone willing to take responsibility, happy to play in unfamiliar positions if it benefits the team, the first to offer support to team-mates, and a positive influence in the dressing room.

Bruno Fernandes scored for Portugal in their Nations League win in Wales

Bruno Fernandes' alarming drop off in form has been one of the most noticeable features of the current campaign.

The Portugal playmaker has been a shadow of the star who scooped all the player of the year awards last season and broke the Premier League assist record.

He was axed for the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after criticising Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League humiliation by Como and seems to be affected by concerns around his future - his contract also expires in the summer, although United are almost certain to trigger their one-year option on the 32-year-old - and the summer arrival of Youri Tielemans.

For the short term at least, Pochettino must decide whether to pick Fernandes in his favoured number 10 role and work around that, or drop him deeper, as Ruben Amorim did, or play him wide, which has not brought the best out of him.

Why does Pochettino keep lemons in his office?

Fernandes' status affects other areas. Carrick never seemed convinced by Andrey Santos, a £50m summer arrival from Chelsea. But with £70m Carlos Baleba out for an extended period, a partner needs to be found in midfield for Kobbie Mainoo.

Tielemans did not seem to have the running ability for the role, and Amorim wouldn't pick Mainoo with Fernandes.

Further forward, with Benjamin Sesko out, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo have tended to be used in the number nine role. But Cunha likes to drop deep, while, after a bright start to the season, Mbeumo has scored twice in his past 12 appearances.

Neither Shea Lacey nor Harry Amass have started a Premier League game this season. Both caught the eye on England Under-20 duty during the international break. Pochettino has history for giving young players a chance and the pair could benefit from that.

Manchester United co-chair Avram Glazer and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe have been the subject of numerous supporter protests and chants

There is one issue Pochettino mentioned in his interview he will soon discover requires delicate handling.

United's match-going fans have stood by every manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired. There is no reason to think that will change now.

However, their relationship with the club's ownership is fractured, possibly beyond repair. Fresh accounts to 30 September show the club's overall debt remains more than £1.1bn and a further £14.5m was spent on finance costs in the previous quarter.

This fuels discontent in the stands, already heightened because of various ticketing measures, none of which are viewed by most supporters as being positive.

"We need to be united," said Pochettino.

"Chemistry is really important, chemistry between us and the staff and the fans and the players, the directors, the owners and everything."

Ubushinwa, Uburusiya na Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika vyasohoye itangazo rusangi ryemeza ko bigiye gukomeza gukorana mu gukingira umutekano w'isi, kugabanya ingorane ziva ku birwanisho ruhonyanganda vy'ubumara (canke vya nikleyeri) no gutsimbataza umwumvikano hagati yavyo.

Ivyo ni bimwe mu vyumvikanyweko mu nama y'imbonekarimwe yahuje Perezida Xi Jinping, Perezida Vladimir Putin na Perezida Donald Trump.

Iyo nama yabereye i Shenzhen mu Bushinwa, mu gihe isi ihanzwe n'ibibazo bikomeye vy'umutekano n'amatati hagati y'ibihugu, yarangijwe n'itangazo ryiswe "Itangazo ry'Amahoro", ryashimikiye ahanini ku nyungu rusangi hagati y'ivyo bihugu, aho kwibanda ku gutorera umuti intambara zirangwa irya n'ino kw'isi.

Ikintu nyamukuru cavuye muri iyo nama ni uko abo bategetsi biyemeje kwirinda ko hoba intambara ya nikleyeri.

Mw'itangazo rusangi ryabo, bavuze ko ata "ruhande na rumwe rushobora gutsinda intambara ya nikleyeri" kandi ko "itegerezwa kutazigera irwanwa."

Biyemeje kandi gukomeza ibiganiro bigamije kugabanya ingorane zijanye n'ivyo birwanisho no guhagarika ikwiragira ryavyo.

Perezida Xi Jinping yavuze ko ivyo birwanisho ari "inkota y'ibiza imanitse hejuru ya kiremwamuntu", asigura ko bikwiye kuzokurwaho burundu.

Perezida Donald Trump na we yashimikiye ku kamaro ko gukorana hagati y'ivyo bihugu mu kurwanya ingorane ziterwa n'ikwirakwira ryavyo kw'isi yose.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Abakuru b'ibi bihugu rutura baganiriye kandi ku kibazo c'intunganywa n'ihanahana ry'ibitoro, ibi bigashobora kugira ico bihinduye ku masoko ntanganguvu kw'isi.

Vyavuze kandi ko bishigikiye ubudahangarwa bw'abategetsi barongoye ibihugu imbere y'inzego zimwe zimwe mpuzamakungu. Iri tangazo rusangi rivuga ko Sentare Mpuzamakungu Mpanavyaha (CPI/ICC) hamwe n'izindi nzego zisa na yo zidategerezwa "gukoresha nabi ububasha zahawe". Muri vyo, nta na kimwe kiri muri iyo sentare.

Ibinyamakuru vyegamiye reta mu Bushinwa vyerekanye ko iyo nama isa n'iyagenze neza cane mu rwego rwa diporomasi.

Bisubiramwo amajambo ya Xi Jinping avuga ko ibiganiro "vyabaye vyiza, vyubaka kandi vyavuyemwo ivyiza vyinshi".

Yongeyeko ko abo bategetsi bumvukanye ko ibihugu rutura bikwiye kwubaha impungenge z'ibindi bihugu ku mutekano wavyo, bashimangira ko kubandanya ibiganiro ari yo nzira ishikana ku mahoro.

Abategetsi b'Uburusiya na bo nyene bashimye uko iyo nama yagenze, aho umushikiranganji w'imigenderanire n'ayandi makungu Sergei Lavrov hamwe n'umujenama w'umukuru w'igihugu Yuri Ushakov bavuze ko ibiganiro vyabaye "vyiza".

Hagati aho, umuvugizi wa Kremlin (ibiro vy'umukuru w'igihugu c'Uburusiya), Dmitry Peskov, yavuze ko intambara yo muri Ukraine itari mu bibazo nyamukuru vyategerezwa kuganirwako.

Abihweza ibintu n'ibindi babona ko umwumvikano hagati ya Donald Trump, Xi Jinping na Vladimir Putin ari kirumara mu bibazo bihanze isi.

Kirill Babaev, umukuru w'Ikigo c'ubushakashatsi ku Bushinwa na Aziya (Institute of China and Contemporary Asia), yabwiye umunyamakuru Leanna Byrne ategura ikiganiro World Business Express ca BBC ko "gukomeza ubucuti burama" hagati ya Trump, Xi na Putin ari ikintu gihambaye mu mu guhanahana amakuru, hamwe no kutorera umuti amatati kw'isi.

Kigali is preparing to host one of its biggest combat sports events yet, with the third edition of Kigali Fight Night set to bring together professional boxers from across Africa at BK Arena on December 10, 2026.

Organised by Silverback Sports, the event is expected to attract about 4,000 spectators, marking a major step in the growth of a competition that began as a local professional boxing showcase and is now seeking to establish itself as a platform for African talent.

This year’s edition will form part of a 12-day Kigali Fight Weekend, organised in collaboration with PFL Africa. The programme will feature two major events: Kigali Fight Night on December 10 and the PFL Africa Finals on December 12, giving the city a wider combat sports programme aimed at attracting athletes, fans and visitors from across the continent.

The move to BK Arena reflects the event’s growing ambitions, with organisers expecting a larger audience, expanded production and increased exposure for boxers from East Africa and other parts of the continent.

The event will feature several high-profile matchups, including a headline bout between Jerry Katamba and Mugunge Augustin, both from Goma in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Rwanda’s Aimable H is scheduled to face Tanzania’s Chappo Mawe, while Cameroon’s Jean Junior will take on Rwandan boxer Mugisha Emma. Other fighters from Kenya, Gabon and Nigeria are also expected to feature.

The organisers say the event is intended to give African boxers more opportunities to compete professionally, build their careers and gain exposure beyond their home countries.

“Our vision for Kigali Fight Night has always been bigger than organising boxing matches. We want to build a platform where African fighters can compete at the highest level, gain the recognition they deserve and develop real professional careers,” said Bashir Ntwari, Chief Executive Officer of Silverback Sports.

He added that the move to BK Arena, together with the partnership with PFL Africa and RwandAir, would help expand the event’s reach and create opportunities for fighters across the continent.

Kigali Fight Night made its debut on November 8, 2025, at Zaria Court in Kigali, bringing together professional and amateur boxers from Rwanda, Nigeria, Tanzania, Gabon, Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The inaugural event featured 11 bouts, including six professional fights and five amateur contests. Among the professional winners were Rwanda’s Frank Kazungu, Nigeria’s David Akintola and Precious Anine, Gabon’s Kingbo Hans, DR Congo’s Daniella Mureketsi and Jerry Katamba, and Cameroon’s Tamba Merlin.

The second edition, held on March 28, 2026, at the Kigali Convention Centre roundabout, expanded the competition’s regional reach, attracting fighters from several African countries.

One of the night’s standout performances came from Cameroon’s Tamba Merlin, who knocked out Tanzania’s Kivu Karume in the second round to claim victory in the final bout. Rwanda’s Aimable Hagenimana also thrilled home supporters, defeating DR Congo’s Muhindo Vianney Bahati by a 17–15 judges’ decision.

The growth from the inaugural event at Zaria Court to the larger BK Arena venue signals the organisers’ ambition to develop Kigali Fight Night into a recognised continental boxing property.

The third edition will also benefit from a partnership with national carrier RwandAir as its official airline sponsor. Under the arrangement, fans travelling to Kigali can access a 20% discount on flights using the promotional code KFN20, subject to applicable booking conditions.

The partnership is expected to support efforts to attract international visitors, with the organisers pointing to potential benefits for hotels, restaurants, transport operators and other businesses serving visitors.

For Jermaine Burke, founder of Dubai-based Universal Sports and Chief Commercial Officer of Silverback Sports, the long-term opportunity goes beyond staging individual fights.

“East Africa has enormous potential for boxing, and we believe the next generation of champions can emerge from this region if young athletes are given the right opportunities,” Burke said.

He noted that developing the sport requires more than organising competitions, arguing that young boxers need access to professional training, regular contests and pathways into sustainable careers.

Through its Africa Fight Night vision, Silverback Sports hopes to connect athletes, promoters, broadcasters, sponsors and audiences while attracting investment into professional boxing across the continent.

With the December event bringing together boxing and MMA under the wider Kigali Fight Weekend programme, organisers are positioning the city as a growing destination for major African combat sports events.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty of all eight counts against him in a Florida court on Wednesday

A Florida pastor has been found guilty of a number of charges relating to the assassination of the Haitian President Jovenel Moïse.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a dual US-Haitian national, was convicted of all eight charges against him, including conspiracy to kill or kidnap a person. He faces a potential sentence of life in prison.

The 67-year-old was accused of being involved in a plot to replace Moïse as Haiti's president with himself in 2021, allegedly so he could award lucrative contracts to a Florida-based security outfit once in place.

The murder of Moïse has left Haiti without a leader for five years. That political vacuum has intensified gang violence in the impoverished Caribbean nation.

A presidential election is scheduled for next year and Moïse's wife, Martine, who was injured in the attack that killed her husband, announced this week that she intended to stand.

Sanon was found guilty on Wednesday following an eight-week trial in federal court in Miami, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner. His lawyer said he maintains his innocence and that he intends to appeal against the verdict, it reports.

Prosecutors said Sanon had "political aspirations" in Haiti and, in April 2021, met several other co-conspirators to devise a plan to oust Moïse in an armed raid on the presidential palace in the capital, Port-au-Prince.

Among them were the heads of the companies Counter Terrorist Unit Federal Academy and Counter Terrorist Unit Security - collectively referred to as CTU - who would finance the coup in exchange for government contracts for infrastructure projects, and to provide security forces and equipment.

A few months later, the other conspirators realised that Sanon had "neither the constitutional qualifications nor the popular support" to become Haiti's president and so shifted to another candidate, the US Department of Justice said.

At the same time, the plot had developed from one to forcibly remove Moïse from office to assassinating him, investigators said.

Dozens of people have been implicated in the conspiracy, which prosecutors said involved co-ordinating funding for and delivering weapons and mercenaries to Haiti to carry out the attack.

On 6 July that year, a group of Colombian mercenaries entered the presidential palace and killed Moïse. His wife, who was also injured in the attack, said at the time that the assailants had "riddled" her husband with bullets.

Jovenel Moïse was gunned down by mercenaries in Haiti's presidential palace in 2021

The successful assassination plot raised questions in Haiti about the relative ease with which the mercenaries were able to gain access to the president.

The country - the poorest in the Americas - has been ravaged by gang violence for years, but Moïse's assassination ushered in a period of worsening instability that emboldened gangs and prompted the deployment of a multinational force.

However, this has struggled to penetrate areas where gangs hold sway and more than 5,700 people have been killed or injured in the year to 11 September, the UN said last month.

Sanon and several other co-conspirators were arrested by Haitian authorities, while three mercenaries were killed in a gun battle with police. Eighteen people were transferred to Florida in September to stand trial over the plot.

Four men, including the heads of the CTU, were convicted of their role earlier this year. Sanon had been scheduled to be tried with them, but his case was delayed due to health reasons, according to CBS.

Sanon was born in Haiti but moved to the US as a teenager. He told the court he had worked in churches in Haitian immigrant communities in several parts of the US including Florida, US media report.

MN202611_kdrwb9kss3.t:
Trump greets 'my friend' Putin ahead of meeting with Xi

US President Donald Trump and his Russian and Chinese counterparts Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have issued a "joint declaration of peace" following historic trilateral talks.

The three leaders met for 90 minutes in China's south-eastern city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

While the presidents have previously had one-on-one meetings, these are their first trilateral talks.

In the declaration, they said "nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought" and that the countries planned to increase the production and supply of petroleum. They also said they were "committed to reform the UN" to respond more effectively to global challenges.

Thursday's statement also flagged the issue of immunity enjoyed by state officials and said "they agreed that the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction".

While in China, Trump also met Putin ahead of the trilateral, in their first meeting since August 2025, where the US president greeted his Russian counterpart as his "friend".

He also spoke with Xi in a separate conversation, describing the pair's relationship as "very special".

Beyond the warmth and shared niceties, however, the three men had different goals and motivations for the sit-down.

This is a remarkable diplomatic moment for China's Xi - but it comes with pitfalls

The opening remarks of the trilateral gave some indication about what was to be discussed during the closed-door meeting.

Before giving the floor to his fellow leaders, Xi said that "positive interaction among major powers is not a matter of choice, but a mandatory requirement".

Putin followed this by highlighting a shared interest in ending the Ukraine war and said the conversation would also touch on food and energy security.

China has officially remained neutral since Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, rejecting accusations from Kyiv and its allies that it has been tacitly supporting Moscow, including by exporting dual-use technology used by the Russian military.

Beijing has also repeatedly called for negotiations and a political settlement while avoiding condemnation of Russia's aggression.

Meanwhile, Trump closed by saying the presidents of three of the world's largest countries have a "special responsibility" to maintain productive dialogue.

"Too often past leaders have avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements," he said, adding: "We feel the opposite."

Trump referenced the three countries' nuclear capabilities and said they are "uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth".

It is "vital" that they co-operate to "combat the threat of nuclear proliferation in other countries around the world", he said, adding: "That's what we're doing in Iran."

"We're not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon".

Trump then turned to Ukraine and said he and Putin have had a "long discussion" on the conflict there already.

He added that Putin "and I hope the other side, would like to see an end to that war".

Putin addressed the media following the trilateral meeting and described it as an "important chapter in the history of diplomacy".

He said Ukraine and Europe were not yet ready to make compromises to resolve the conflict in Ukraine - but he said Russia had invited EU representatives to Moscow to better understand Europe's position.

As the talks were under way in China, and even as Putin was holding his press conference claiming to be ready for peace, Ukraine's capital Kyiv was under attack from Russian drones.

Putin has repeatedly rejected all ceasefire offers from Ukraine, insisting on his maximalist demands which Kyiv and its European allies say are tantamount to de facto capitulation of Ukraine.

In Shenzhen, the Kremlin leader also vowed a "far more painful" retaliation in response to Ukrainian attacks on the bridge connecting Russia to Ukraine's occupied peninsula of Crimea. A missile and drone attack on Tuesday destroyed its central road section.

There was no mention from Putin of almost five years of Russian attacks on power plants, bridges and residential buildings in Ukraine.

The Russian president also directly addressed comparisons between his meeting with Trump and Xi and the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the leaders of the Soviet Union, Britain and the US met towards the end of World War Two.

"Nobody divided up the world at Yalta. It simply codified the realities that had emerged after WW2.

"And when it comes to today's conflicts, the realities on the ground will have to be accepted."

The Kremlin released a video showing Putin leaving the summit venue and saying goodbye to Xi.

"Thank you for organising this," Putin said. "I don't think anyone even expected everything to go so well."

Meanwhile, China's president described his meeting with Putin and Trump as "positive, constructive, and highly productive", according to the country's state broadcaster CCTV.

It added that Xi recalled "the history of fighting side-by-side during WW2", as the three leaders emphasised the importance of "cherishing the hard-won peace".

Thursday's trilateral meeting was reportedly the idea of Putin.

Some Russian newspapers called it a "diplomatic victory" as after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine many Western leaders were trying to isolate him.

The summit also marked the first time since Russia's war in Ukraine began that Putin took part in an international gathering attended by leaders from countries including Canada, Japan and Australia.

Blackpool have sacked head coach Ian Evatt after a year in charge following a run of one win and six defeats in their past 10 league games.

Evatt's final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon , leaving the Tangerines immediately above the League One relegation zone.

That defeat, however, came after the 45-year-old said his squad had been decimated by a sickness bug during their trip to the capital.

In a statement, the club thanked Evatt for his efforts and said Steve Thompson will take charge for Saturday's game against Wigan Athletic.

Blackpool appointed Evatt, who won promotion from League One and the Championship during seven years as a centre-back for the club, as Steve Bruce's successor in October 2025.

During a six-year playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made over 250 appearances for the Seasiders - however he departs the club on his 45th birthday.

On arrival as a manager, a tally of 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 lifted them out of the relegation zone, although they lost 10 and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again as this season continued.

Speaking after their defeat by Mansfield in October, Evatt said he had "a huge amount of confidence" in his ability because of his record.

Evatt guided Barrow to the 2019-20 National League title in his first managerial role, then won promotion from League One with Bolton Wanderers the following season.

Wanderers went on to lift the 2022-23 EFL Trophy and reached the third-tier play-offs in consecutive seasons under Evatt, losing in the final in his final full campaign in 2023-24.
